The film splits into a first half about training and a second about a massacre, and the transition between them is deliberate and unexplained. Directed by Stanley Kubrick.
movies|full-metal-jacket.shortSynopsis: A recruit is trained as a Marine in three stages and then abandoned in a city that has been emptied of civilians.

movies|funny-girl.synopsis: A girl from Brooklyn takes a name from Ziegfeld Follies and talks her way into it, and then marries the man who made her, and has to live in a house where everything is a performance. Directed by William Wyler, and the film that won Barbra Streisand her only Oscar.
movies|funny-girl.shortSynopsis: A Brooklyn girl talks her way into the Ziegfeld Follies, then marries the man who cast her.

movies|fury.synopsis: In April 1945 a tank crew in a broken-down Sherman is given orders to keep a church in a German town, and the film follows the four days in which they hold it. Written and directed by David Ayer, and the film is about what happens to a crew of ordinary men given a task they cannot win.
movies|fury.shortSynopsis: A Sherman tank crew is ordered to hold a German town for four days in April 1945, with no infantry support.

movies|gallipoli.synopsis: Two Tasmanian men enlist in the Australian army, are told they are going to fight a Turkish cannon, and are put in a campaign that goes badly, and one of them is told to write home from a place he is not. Directed by Peter Weir, and the film that ended the Anzac legend in Australian cinema.
movies|gallipoli.shortSynopsis: Two Tasmanians enlist for Gallipoli, believing they will fight a cannon, and are sent into a campaign that goes badly.

movies|get-out.synopsis: A young Black photographer visits his white girlfriend's family estate for the weekend and is made to play tennis, undergo a medical examination and watch a series of Black people, and one of whom cannot move. Written and directed by Jordan Peele, and the film that was called a horror film and was a political one.
movies|get-out.shortSynopsis: A young Black photographer visiting his girlfriend's family estate is made the subject of a series of tests.

movies|ghost.synopsis: A man and a woman whose apartment was the subject of a real siege takes two crooks' idea from a paperback, is shot, and comes back for his girlfriend, and stays in the world. Directed by Jerry Zucker, and the film that made 'Who ya gonna call' the template for a line of them.
movies|ghost.shortSynopsis: A man comes back for his girlfriend after robbers kill him, and stays around to finish the job.

movies|ghostbusters.synopsis: Four academics with no money build a containment unit out of a converted firehouse basement, lose their jobs for it, and go into business, and the first customer is a woman in a hotel who is not dead. Directed by Ivan Reitman, and the film that made its theme song the most performed in cinema.
movies|ghostbusters.shortSynopsis: Four academics build a ghost-catching device, lose their jobs, and start a business out of a firehouse.

movies|gladiator.synopsis: A Roman general is betrayed by the emperor he served, sold to slavery, fights his way through the arena circuit, and is offered the empire by people who want to remove the current one, and the only thing he actually wants is his family. Directed by Ridley Scott, and the film that made the arena format legible to modern cinema.
movies|gladiator.shortSynopsis: A betrayed Roman general is sold into slavery, fights in the arena, and is offered the empire by those who want to take it.

movies|glass-onion.synopsis: An amateur sleuth turns up to a private island where a billionaire has assembled a handful of people, one of whom has just been killed, and the play nobody has seen the solution to is the murder mystery, which is being performed in front of them the whole time. Directed by Rian Johnson, following Knives Out.
movies|glass-onion.shortSynopsis: A murder mystery is being performed on an island while a billionaire's guests are killed according to the play's plan.

movies|gone-baby-gone.synopsis: A detective and a state-appointed child advocate go to a working-class town to find a missing girl, and each has decided what the truth is worth, and the ending is the only one of the three possible. Written by Aaron Stockard, and directed by Denis Villeneuve in his first American film.
movies|gone-baby-gone.shortSynopsis: A detective and a child advocate search for a missing girl and arrive at opposite conclusions about her.

movies|gone-girl.synopsis: A man reports his wife missing on their fifth wedding anniversary, and the publicity makes the marriage a national event, and the woman reappears and explains the five years. Written by Aaron Guffanti and adapted from a novel by Gillian Flynn, who wrote both the novel and the screenplay.
movies|gone-girl.shortSynopsis: A man reports his wife missing and the case becomes a media event, and when she returns she has her own account.

movies|good-will-hunting.synopsis: A shipyard janitor in South Boston with an extraordinary gift for numbers is wrongly suspected of a crime, is required to see a therapist, and lies to her for six sessions. Directed by Gus Van Sant, and the film that won Robin Williams the Oscar he said he did not want.
movies|good-will-hunting.shortSynopsis: A gifted South Boston janitor is required to see a therapist and spends six sessions lying to her.

movies|goodfellas.synopsis: A Brooklyn kid works his way into the New York mob over thirty years, and the film is narrated by him and ends with him giving drug counselling in California, saying that everything after a certain point was downhill. Directed by Martin Scorsese, from a non-fiction book by Nicholas Pileggi.
movies|goodfellas.shortSynopsis: A Brooklyn kid works into the New York mob over thirty years, and narrates his own decline.

movies|grave-of-the-fireflies.synopsis: In 1945 Japan a fourteen-year-old boy and his little sister are left to manage after their mother dies, and he goes through fire for her, and the fireflies are the title. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, from a 1967 Akiyuki Nosaka novella, and often named among the most devastating war films ever made.
movies|grave-of-the-fireflies.shortSynopsis: A boy and his little sister are left to manage in 1945 Japan after their mother dies, and he goes through fire for her.

movies|gravity.synopsis: Two astronauts are doing a spacewalk and everything is destroyed, and one of them is left attached to the outside of the station and has to find her way back in. Written and directed by Alfonso Cuarón, and the majority of the film is a single unbroken shot.
movies|gravity.shortSynopsis: Two astronauts are on a spacewalk when everything is destroyed, and one is stranded on the outside of the station.

movies|grease.synopsis: A greaser boy and a girl who wants to be a cheerleader in 1960s California have to be a good year, and the school fair is the testing ground, and the ending has a deliberate anachronism in it. Directed by Randal Kleiser, adapted from the stage musical.
movies|grease.shortSynopsis: A greaser and a cheerleader in 1960s California have to get through the school year and the dance.

movies|grizzly-man.synopsis: A man spent twenty-seven years living among Alaskan grizzlies, most of it alone, and the film is assembled from his own footage and his own recorded journals. Werner Herzog narrates, and did so without the narrator's cooperation, and the two records do not agree.
movies|grizzly-man.shortSynopsis: A documentary built from a man's own footage and journals of twenty-seven years living among Alaskan grizzlies.

movies|groundhog-day.synopsis: A weatherman on assignment in Punxsutawney is stuck on the second of February, and learns that nothing he does has a consequence, and uses that first for the worst things and then for the rest. Directed by Harold Ramis, and the film's original ending is the one that should be remembered.
movies|groundhog-day.shortSynopsis: A weatherman is stuck on the second of February and learns that nothing he does has a consequence.

movies|hacksaw-ridge.synopsis: A Seventh-day Adventist medic refuses to carry a weapon and is sent to Okinawa as a conscientious objector, and insists on going down into the wounded under fire when the line is told to retreat, and at the time the US Army's own history had no record of a person who had done so. Directed by Mel Gibson.
movies|hacksaw-ridge.shortSynopsis: An Adventist medic who refuses to carry a rifle goes into the wounded under fire on Okinawa.

movies|hairspray.synopsis: In Baltimore in 1962, a plus-sized teenager who can sing wants to be on a local television dance show, and the girl she likes has to be white, and the film is about the schools separating along colour lines the same week she goes on television. Directed by John Waters, from his own stage musical.
movies|hairspray.shortSynopsis: In Baltimore 1962, a plus-sized teenager wants to be on a television dance show, in a week the city desegregates.

movies|halloween.synopsis: A six-year-old's Halloween murder goes unsolved, and five years later the killer comes back to a town where nobody is looking for him. The film is not a slasher picture; it follows a group of teenagers who spend the night trying to find each other rather than trying to survive.
movies|halloween.shortSynopsis: An unsolved Halloween murder is repeated five years later, and the killer knows nobody is looking for him.

movies|harry-potter-and-the-prisoner-of-.synopsis: A student finds out he is a wizard, and in his third year at school he is taught a spell that lets him go back in time, which he uses to save someone who died, and the consequences reach him in a way he does not expect. Directed by Alfonso Cuarón, and the first film that looked like the books rather than the previous two.
movies|harry-potter-and-the-prisoner-of-.shortSynopsis: In his third year at wizard school, a student is taught a time-turning spell and uses it to undo a death.

movies|harry-potter-and-the-sorcerers-st.synopsis: An eleven-year-old who does not know he is a wizard is delivered to a school, and finds that the headmaster's most precious possession is guarded in a chamber three floors down under a set of traps his friends can work out. Directed by Chris Columbus, from the first of J. K. Rowling's books.
movies|harry-potter-and-the-sorcerers-st.shortSynopsis: An eleven-year-old is told he is a wizard, goes to a school, and works out how to get past the three floors of traps.

movies|heat.synopsis: A career thief and the detective who has been trying to catch him sit down in a diner and talk about the two of them, and the film then spends its last twenty minutes on a bank robbery neither man is willing to go into. Directed by Michael Mann, and the conversation at the diner is the film's reputation.
movies|heat.shortSynopsis: A career thief and the detective hunting him meet in a diner, and later both work the same bank job.

movies|hell-or-high-water.synopsis: Two brothers in Wyoming rob banks, and the older one is in debt to a bookmaker who is also their mother's carer, and the film follows them through a robbery that goes wrong while the debt is being paid off. Written and directed by David Mackenzie.
movies|hell-or-high-water.shortSynopsis: Two brothers in Wyoming rob banks, and the older one is paying off a debt to the man caring for their mother.

movies|hereditary.synopsis: A woman whose husband has recently died begins to suspect that her daughter has some kind of influence over her, and is right, and the film turns in its final minutes into something else entirely. Written and directed by Ari Aster, and the first half plays as a domestic drama.
movies|hereditary.shortSynopsis: A grieving mother suspects her daughter of influencing her, and the film turns in its final minutes.

movies|hidalgo.synopsis: In 1890 a Texas rancher takes a horse-racing job in a quarter-horse race across the desert from El Paso to a city named for an old massacre, with his daughter riding with him. Directed by Phillip Noyce, and the film is about a horse and a heat that is at times a real danger.
movies|hidalgo.shortSynopsis: An 1890 Texas rancher rides a quarter horse across the desert to Ciudad Juárez, racing a friend who is not a friend.

movies|high-noon.synopsis: A marshal who has just married walks out of town because the men who killed his predecessor are coming back, and the film spends ninety minutes in the midday before they arrive, with everybody leaving the square one at a time. Directed by Fred Zinnemann, and the running time of the confrontation is the point.
movies|high-noon.shortSynopsis: A marshal who has just married waits alone in a town square for the men who killed his predecessor.

movies|home-alone.synopsis: A boy is left behind while his family flies to Paris and defends his house from two burglars across a sequence of increasingly elaborate traps, and the film's real subject turns out to be his older brother. Directed by Chris Columbus, and the film that made Macaulay Culkin a star.
movies|home-alone.shortSynopsis: An eight-year-old is left home alone at Christmas and defends the house from two burglars with elaborate traps.

movies|honey-i-shrunk-the-kids.synopsis: An inventor shrinks his own children by accident, and then his wife by accident, and has to work with a neighbour's children to find them, and the film's adult plot is a subplot about a neighbour selling the house. Directed by Joe Johnston, and the first family film to have a genuinely threatening edge.
movies|honey-i-shrunk-the-kids.shortSynopsis: An inventor shrinks his children by accident and has to find them before their mother gets home.

movies|hook.synopsis: Peter Pan grows up and forgets, his children are taken to Neverland because he will not play, and he has to go back, and there the pirate hook is a real hand and there is a battle. Directed by Steven Spielberg, and the film's argument is that growing up means going back to play.
movies|hook.shortSynopsis: A father who forgot he was Peter Pan goes to Neverland to get his children back from Captain Hook.

movies|hoop-dreams.synopsis: A documentary following two boys in Chicago from age eleven, both talented enough for college basketball scouts to come to their games, one of whom is let down and one of whom is not. Directed by Steve James, and the ending is the one nobody in the film was told about.
movies|hoop-dreams.shortSynopsis: A documentary following two talented Chicago boys from age eleven as college scouts come to see them play.

movies|hoosiers.synopsis: A man returns to the small Indiana town where he was once a coach, to coach its basketball team, and is hired partly on the recommendation of a nineteen-year-old who is the best player anyone has seen there. Directed by Barry Levinson, and Gene Hackman plays the returning coach.
movies|hoosiers.shortSynopsis: A man returns to a small Indiana town to coach basketball, on the word of a nineteen-year-old who plays like no one there has seen.

movies|how-to-train-your-dragon.synopsis: A Viking who does not fit in and does not want to fight dragons has one left, injures it, and befriends it, and then has to explain to a village that has lost its food source why he is right. Directed by Chris Sanders and Dean DeBlois, and the film that started the studio's run.
movies|how-to-train-your-dragon.shortSynopsis: A Viking who cannot fight dragons befriends the one he wounded, and has to persuade a village he is right.

movies|howls-moving-castle.synopsis: A hatmaker is cursed into old age by a witch and goes to find the wizard who did it, and lives in his castle while the war comes to them, and the curse is a spell somebody put on her on purpose. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, and nominated for the Academy Award.
movies|howls-moving-castle.shortSynopsis: A hatmaker is cursed into old age by a witch and goes to a wizard's moving castle to ask him to undo it.

movies|icarus.synopsis: A documentary about how the Lance Armstrong doping programme was uncovered, told from the perspective of a cyclist who rode for years beside him and agreed to fake a retirement from the sport to get close. Directed by Bryan Fogel.
movies|icarus.shortSynopsis: A cyclist goes undercover in Lance Armstrong's team to document the doping that ended him.

movies|identity.synopsis: Ten strangers are stranded at a roadside motel during a storm with a killer among them, and the film is an extended homage to the opening of Psycho. Directed by Alexandre Aja, and the twist at the end is in the title.
movies|identity.shortSynopsis: Ten strangers are stranded at a motel during a storm with a killer among them.

movies|in-bruges.synopsis: A hitman and the man who picks up the body have a week in Bruges before the head of the IRA wants the money, and the film is about two men who would both rather be somewhere else. Written and directed by Martin McDonagh, and the first film he made in English.
movies|in-bruges.shortSynopsis: A hitman and his partner hide in Bruges with the proceeds of a job nobody wants collected.

movies|in-the-heights.synopsis: In Washington Heights a man runs a neighbourhood grocery and is trying to get a tram line that will change the value of everything his family owns, and the girl he has grown up beside has been lying about where she is from. Directed by Jon M. Chu, and adapted from the stage musical.
movies|in-the-heights.shortSynopsis: A grocer in Washington Heights fights for a tram line that will make his family's land valuable, and his childhood friend has been lying.

movies|in-the-mood-for-love.synopsis: In 1962 Hong Kong, two neighbours whose spouses are having an affair with each other begin to suspect it, and instead of confronting anyone they begin rehearsing what the scenes would have been like, and the film never resolves anything. Written and directed by Wong Kar-wai, and made with a partner who co-wrote and directed it with him.
movies|in-the-mood-for-love.shortSynopsis: In 1962 Hong Kong, two neighbours whose spouses are unfaithful to each other begin rehearsing the scenes they imagine.

movies|inception.synopsis: A thief who steals information from inside people's dreams is offered one last job: put an idea in rather than take one out, and the film is about the difference between a memory and a thought, and about whether anyone comes back. Written and directed by Christopher Nolan.
movies|inception.shortSynopsis: A dream thief is offered one last job: put an idea in a man's head rather than take one out.

movies|indiana-jones-and-the-last-crusad.synopsis: The third and last of the series, in which Indiana's father is found after fifty years in a castle, and the Grail is the prize, and the film ends with a scene set in 1939 that nobody had to be in the story. Directed by Steven Spielberg.
movies|indiana-jones-and-the-last-crusad.shortSynopsis: Indiana Jones has to find his father and the Holy Grail, and the film ends in 1939 for no reason anyone gives.

movies|inside-out.synopsis: A girl is moved to San Francisco and everything in her head has to be rebuilt, and the emotions have to work out who she is now, and the film is a fairly literal diagram of a mind. Written and directed by Pete Docter, with a cast of voice actors doing five jobs each.
movies|inside-out.shortSynopsis: A girl moves house and the five emotions inside her head have to work out who she is now.

movies|insidious.synopsis: A boy looks into a strange world under the house and goes further than he should, and the people searching for him are in danger of going after him, and the family's other child knows more than she is saying. Written and directed by James Wan.
movies|insidious.shortSynopsis: A boy goes into the world under his house, and his family's search for him becomes the danger.

movies|insomnia.synopsis: A detective who has not slept since a murder he is investigating is on a case in a town in Alaska where the sun does not set, and two people are killed overnight in circumstances that do not work. Written and directed by Christopher Nolan, and his second feature.
movies|insomnia.shortSynopsis: A sleep-deprived detective investigates two murders in an Alaskan town where the sun never sets.

movies|interstellar.synopsis: A farmer's son in a dying dust bowl discovers that a wormhole left by humanity can be reached from Earth, and agrees to leave his children to go through it, and the film is about what he comes back to. Written and directed by Christopher Nolan.
movies|interstellar.shortSynopsis: A farmer's son leaves his children to pass through a wormhole in an attempt to save the crops, and comes back years later.

movies|into-the-wild.synopsis: A young man from a wealthy Chicago family gives up college, gives up his savings, and travels alone by bus and freight to Alaska, and dies in a bus wreck at the Bus 142. Directed by Sean Penn, from Jon Krakauer's book, and the film ends with a bus that arrives somewhere and the narration asks who gets on it.
movies|into-the-wild.shortSynopsis: A wealthy young man gives up everything and travels alone to Alaska, and dies at a frozen bus stop.

movies|into-the-woods.synopsis: A baker and his wife wish for a child, the child becomes a girl who is everything they hoped for, and the girl wishes to be fair and the witch takes her, and to get her back the baker has to stop wanting. Directed by Rob Marshall, from Sondheim and James Lapine's stage musical.
movies|into-the-woods.shortSynopsis: A baker's daughter wishes to be fair, is taken by a witch, and he must give up wanting to get her back.

movies|invincible.synopsis: The son of a comics publisher who is a fan of the book's character becomes that character, and uses what the fictional version could do, and the film's question is how much of it is the father. Directed by Philip J. Fry, and the story is told twice, once through the son's eyes and once without.
movies|invincible.shortSynopsis: A young man's father runs a comics imprint, and the son becomes the hero of its title character, and we see it both ways.

movies|it.synopsis: A group of children in a Maine town lose two of their own to a shape-shifting monster, and decide to destroy it, and the adults refuse to believe any of it, and the film's success is largely down to the chemistry of children not being believed. Directed by Andy Muschietti, from Stephen King's first novel.
movies|it.shortSynopsis: Children in a Maine town lose friends to a shape-shifting monster, and no adult will believe them.

movies|it-follows.synopsis: A young woman has sex with a man and finds that something is following her, and it is passed on by sex, and the film is about the two people who can do something about it, one of whom has read enough to know what to look for. Written and directed by David Robert Mitchell.
movies|it-follows.shortSynopsis: A young woman finds something following her after a one-night stand, and two young men try to identify what it is.

movies|jagged-edge.synopsis: A figure skater in Detroit kills her husband, and a lawyer defends her on a theory about the state of mind she was in, while another skater who is about to compete in the same event is told something she cannot use. Directed by Richard Marquand, and the first film the two leads appeared in together.
movies|jagged-edge.shortSynopsis: A Detroit skater kills her husband and a lawyer defends her on a theory about her mental state.

movies|jarhead.synopsis: A Marine in the first Gulf War watches a war in which he never fights, standing in a line of men waiting, and returns home to find the work is not there. Adapted by the writer from his own memoir, and deliberately denies the audience the combat footage the title implies.
movies|jarhead.shortSynopsis: A US Marine serves in the Gulf War in a long waiting game, and comes home to find no work waiting for him.

movies|jaws.synopsis: A resort town decides it cannot afford to close its beaches, so a marine biologist is asked to kill a great white, and he finds the animal is not where they think and is not doing what they think. Directed by Steven Spielberg, and the film that is built so the shark is seen least often and is the most frightening.
movies|jaws.shortSynopsis: A resort town will not close its beaches, so a marine biologist is asked to deal with a great white shark.

movies|jerry-maguire.synopsis: A sports agent is fired for telling a client what he should hear, and takes one client with him, and writes the letter the film is named after, and has eleven days to get his career back. Written and directed by Cameron Crowe, and the film that made Tom Cruise a star and a producer.
movies|jerry-maguire.shortSynopsis: A fired sports agent takes one client, writes the letter the film is named after, and has eleven days to get back.

movies|jiro-dreams-of-sushi.synopsis: A documentary about an eight-seat sushi counter in a Tokyo basement and the eighty-year-old man who runs it and his son, who spends a year in the kitchen doing nothing but pressing rice. Directed by David Gelb, and the subject was too ill to travel to the premiere.
movies|jiro-dreams-of-sushi.shortSynopsis: A documentary about an eighty-year-old sushi master in a Tokyo basement and the year his son spent there.

movies|john-wick.synopsis: A retired hitman comes out of retirement when someone kills his dog and steals his car, and the crime turns out to be the underworld's trigger for a large reward, and he has to take it back. Written and directed by Derek Kolstad, and the film that made the gun fu of a Hong Kong tradition into a genre again.
movies|john-wick.shortSynopsis: A retired hitman comes back when his dog is killed and his car stolen, for a reward he did not want.

movies|journey-to-the-center-of-the-eart.synopsis: A professor, his nephew and three other people go down a shaft in Iceland into a world that has its own weather and its own animals, and the film ends on an ancient continent. Directed by Brad Silberling, from Jules Verne, and the practical effects are the reason to watch it.
movies|journey-to-the-center-of-the-eart.shortSynopsis: A professor and four others descend a shaft in Iceland into a world with its own weather and its own animals.

movies|jumanji.synopsis: A board game that four children find in a attic does not work like a game, and whatever is rolled comes true, and the film is mostly the children arguing about rules. Directed by Joe Johnston, and the film is structured as a series of game turns with the adults drawn into the board.
movies|jumanji.shortSynopsis: A board game in an attic does not work like a game, and everything rolled comes true.

movies|jurassic-park.synopsis: A billionaire opens a park of cloned dinosaurs, and the four people he takes to endorse it are the ones who have to get everyone out, and the security is being run by a man who has been embezzling. Directed by Steven Spielberg, from Michael Crichton's novel.
movies|jurassic-park.shortSynopsis: A dinosaur park's security is being run by a man who has been embezzling, and the guests are the evacuation plan.

movies|kellys-heroes.synopsis: In 1943 a gang of bank robbers, including Kelly and four other men and Kelly's mother, dress as soldiers in an American town where the real soldiers are about to arrive, and the last hour is the two sides looking for each other. Directed by Brian G. Hutton, with Gene Kelly and Donald Sutherland.
movies|kellys-heroes.shortSynopsis: A 1943 bank robbery gang dressed as soldiers hides in a town where the real soldiers are about to arrive.

movies|kill-bill-vol-1.synopsis: A woman who was left for dead on her wedding day comes out of a coma and goes after the five men responsible, one at a time, each in a setting chosen to be as awkward for him as possible. Written and directed by Quentin Tarantino, and the film deliberately mixes genres between chapters.
movies|kill-bill-vol-1.shortSynopsis: A woman left for dead on her wedding day comes out of a coma and goes after the five men who did it.

movies|kill-the-irishman.synopsis: An IRA member who is questioned for ten years under the Good Friday Agreement and eventually gives up his comrades, and the film is told in the first person as the interrogation. Directed by Jim Sheridan, from the memoirs, and starring Ben Kingsley.
movies|kill-the-irishman.shortSynopsis: An IRA member is interrogated for ten years under the Good Friday Agreement, and eventually talks.

movies|killing-them-softly.synopsis: A hitman in a Los Angeles basement tells a group of robbers who is going to die in the next half hour and why, and the film is one long conversation with a bank robbery going on upstairs. Directed by Andrew Dominik, and the title is the last line of the film.
movies|killing-them-softly.shortSynopsis: A hitman tells a group of robbers in a basement who among them is going to die, while the robbery continues upstairs.

movies|king-kong.synopsis: In 1933 New York, a film crew goes to Skull Island for footage and brings back a giant ape, which is displayed in a theatre and then taken to the city, and the last third of the film is a building. Directed by Peter Jackson.
movies|king-kong.shortSynopsis: A film crew brings a giant ape back from Skull Island, and it is taken to New York in a crane.

movies|knives-out.synopsis: A wealthy crime writer is found dead the morning after his birthday party, and a detective is hired by the family, and it turns out everyone in the house had a motive. Written and directed by Rian Johnson, and the film is deliberately comic in tone.
movies|knives-out.shortSynopsis: A crime writer is found dead after his birthday party, and everyone in the house had a motive.

movies|knocked-up.synopsis: A conservative television producer sleeps with a nightclub dancer and she turns out to be pregnant, and he is not the man he was a week ago. Written and directed by Judd Apatow, and the last twenty minutes is a procedure on a table.
movies|knocked-up.shortSynopsis: A conservative television producer sleeps with a dancer, and finds out a week later that he is going to be a father.

movies|kubo-and-the-two-strings.synopsis: A boy in feudal Japan who is too frightened to go outside, in a deliberately incomplete stop-motion world, goes to find his father's armour, and is helped along the way by a fox, a dragonfly and a beetle who are the story's three strings. Directed by Travis Knight, and Laika's second film.
movies|kubo-and-the-two-strings.shortSynopsis: A boy in a partly finished Japan goes to find his father's armour, helped by a fox, a dragonfly and a beetle.

movies|l-a-confidential.synopsis: In 1953 two Los Angeles police officers, one ideal and one corrupt, are assigned together to a murder, and the film is a set of stories about the city that end in the same place. Written and directed by Curtis Hanson, and the film that made the modern police thriller's template.
movies|l-a-confidential.shortSynopsis: In 1953 Los Angeles, one honest and one corrupt officer investigate a murder and end up holding the same secret.

movies|la-la-land.synopsis: A jazz pianist and an aspiring actress in Los Angeles meet on a fire escape, are happy for a few years, and then one of them is offered a place in a Paris production and has to decide, and the last scene shows what would have happened. Written and directed by Damien Chazelle, and the final shot is over five minutes long.
movies|la-la-land.shortSynopsis: A pianist and an actress meet in Los Angeles, are happy for a few years, and one of them is offered Paris.

movies|labyrinth.synopsis: A teenager whose stepsister has been taken by the Goblin King goes into the Labyrinth to get her back, with a stuffed dog, a bread trail and a man who is a body with two pairs of hands. Directed by Jim Henson, and the film is remembered for the puppetry and for the opening dance number.
movies|labyrinth.shortSynopsis: A teenager goes into a goblin labyrinth to retrieve her stepsister, helped by a dog, bread crumbs and a man in a coat.

movies|layer-cake.synopsis: A London cocaine dealer is given four weeks to clear out what he owes, and spends the time being beaten by organised crime while trying to arrange one last score. Written and directed by Matthew Vaughn, and the film is about a man who has never had a plan and thinks he does.
movies|layer-cake.shortSynopsis: A London drug dealer is given four weeks to clear out what he owes, and spends them being beaten by his suppliers.

movies|legally-blonde.synopsis: A sorority president from Bel-Air is rejected from Harvard Law and decides to go anyway, and finds herself defending a fitness instructor in a murder case, and finds that she is good at it. Written from a novel by Amanda Brown, and the film that made Reese Witherspoon a serious actor.
movies|legally-blonde.shortSynopsis: A Bel-Air sorority president is rejected from Harvard Law, goes anyway, and wins a murder case.

movies|legend.synopsis: The story of the Kray twins told twice, once following each brother, so that the same events are seen as loyalty from one side and as a wall from the other. Written and directed by Brian Helgeland, and Tom Hardy plays both.
movies|legend.shortSynopsis: The Kray twins' story told twice, following each brother, so the same events read as loyalty and as a wall.

movies|leon-the-professional.synopsis: A hitman who retires after refusing a job and taking a girl in with him is asked to do the job he refused, and there is only one person he will take it from. Written and directed by Luc Besson, and the film that established his visual style and Jean Reno's career.
movies|leon-the-professional.shortSynopsis: A retired hitman is asked to do the one job he turned down, and there is only one person he will take it from.

movies|les-miserables.synopsis: In nineteenth-century France, an ex-convict who has been in prison for sixteen years is let out and swears to himself he will never steal again, and the film's ending is a barricade in the Paris streets. Directed by Tom Hooper, from the novel and the musical, and shot partly as a single street sequence.
movies|les-miserables.shortSynopsis: An ex-convict released after sixteen years, and a student barricade in the Paris streets of 1789.

movies|lethal-weapon.synopsis: Two Los Angeles police officers, one reckless and one by the book, are teamed after a widow's husband is killed in a rigged car accident, and the investigation leads them to a former colleague. Directed by Richard Donner, and the film that made Mel Gibson and Danny Glover a pair and made the buddy cop a genre.
movies|lethal-weapon.shortSynopsis: A reckless cop and a careful cop are teamed after a car accident, and the case leads them to a former colleague.

movies|letters-from-iwo-jima.synopsis: A Japanese soldier writes letters to his young son about the campaign on Iwo Jima, in a film told from the Japanese side of a battle the previous year had been filmed from the American one. Directed by Clint Eastwood, from letters discovered after the war that had never been sent.
movies|letters-from-iwo-jima.shortSynopsis: A Japanese soldier writes to his son from Iwo Jima, in a film made from letters found after the war.

movies|life-of-pi.synopsis: A Indian boy is the only survivor of a shipwreck, and spends months on an island with a Bengal tiger, and the last third of the film is a ship searching for him. Directed by Ang Lee, from Yann Martel's novel, and the tiger is real and the water is real.
movies|life-of-pi.shortSynopsis: An Indian boy survives a shipwreck and spends months alone on an island with a Bengal tiger.

movies|little-women.synopsis: The four March sisters come of age in Massachusetts around the Civil War, told through the parts of Louisa May Alcott's novel that Alcott based on her own sisters, including one who wrote. Written and directed by Greta Gerwig.
movies|little-women.shortSynopsis: The four March sisters come of age in Massachusetts around the Civil War, in Alcott's own family.

movies|lock-stock-and-two-smoking-barrel.synopsis: Four young men in a London flat scheme a robbery so they can pay a man who is going to kill one of them, and the plan depends on an old gangster being in on it. Written and directed by Guy Ritchie, and the film that made him a director and introduced Jason Statham and Vinnie Jones.
movies|lock-stock-and-two-smoking-barrel.shortSynopsis: Four young men in a London flat rob a man who is going to kill one of them, and recruit an old gangster to help.

movies|looper.synopsis: In 2074 an assassin kills his target in the future and is then killed by his younger self, who is sent back to do it, and the film works out what happens when that self refuses. Written and directed by Rian Johnson, who had begun as a friend of Bruce Willis and lost the part.
movies|looper.shortSynopsis: An assassin is sent back in time to kill the person he is there to kill, and finds out that person is himself.

movies|love-actually.synopsis: Ten separate stories about people in London finding out how much they need each other, told in parallel and cut between, and the frame is a press conference about a son in a comedy where a boy says the thing about the primary school teacher. Written and directed by Richard Curtis.
movies|love-actually.shortSynopsis: Ten stories about people in London finding out how much they need each other, told in parallel.

movies|mad-max-fury-road.synopsis: In a world without fuel, a man who was a tanker driver joins a war captain's attempt to take a fuel field from the warlord who has it, and the whole chase is one long drive. Directed by George Miller, and the film is a chase sequence that took most of its running time.
movies|mad-max-fury-road.shortSynopsis: In a world without fuel, a former tanker driver joins a war captain's drive to take a fuel field by force.

movies|major-league.synopsis: A baseball team with a payroll of one thousand dollars, owner Lou Brown, makes five deliberately terrible replacements to the roster he is given, and the last game of the season is against a team that has no reason to lose to anyone. Directed by David Ward, and the film that is still quoted by people who have managed anything.
movies|major-league.shortSynopsis: The Cleveland Indians make five terrible signings to a ruined roster, and win a game they had no right to win.

movies|maleficent.synopsis: A fairy is betrayed and put to sleep for sixteen years, and the child who is put to sleep in her place is given to her to raise, and the film is the argument that she is not what she has been called. Directed by Robert Stromberg, and a retelling from the villain's point of view.
movies|maleficent.shortSynopsis: A fairy betrayed and put to sleep raises the princess she was given, and is not what she has been called.

movies|mamma-mia.synopsis: A woman discovers she is about to marry a man she does not love, on a Greek island, and tells her two daughters who the father is, and invites him, and there are two of him. Directed by Phyllida Lloyd, with the ABBA score, and the film is deliberately a holiday.
movies|mamma-mia.shortSynopsis: A woman about to marry the wrong man tells her two daughters who the father is, on a Greek island.

movies|man-on-wire.synopsis: A French wire-walker walked a cable between the two towers of the World Trade Center in 1974, illegally, for twenty-four minutes, and this documentary assembles what he, his friends and the police said afterwards. Directed by James Marsh, and the only film to win both the Sundance Grand Jury Prize and the Oscar for Best Documentary.
movies|man-on-wire.shortSynopsis: A French wire-walker crosses the Twin Towers on a cable for twenty-four minutes, and this is the account afterwards.

movies|manchester-by-the-sea.synopsis: A ship chandler in Massachusetts is told that his brother has died, and has to go and speak to the executor of his will, which is the nephew who was responsible, and who asks to be left alone. Written and directed by Kenneth Lonergan, who said the film is about surviving something.
movies|manchester-by-the-sea.shortSynopsis: A man in Massachusetts has to speak to the nephew he is sure killed his brother, and then bury the brother.

movies|march-of-the-penguins.synopsis: Emperor penguins at the edge of the Antarctic ice breed in the winter, when the sea is frozen for nine months, and the males stand on the ice for two months without eating while the females are at sea. Written and narrated by the ecologist who spent twelve years with them. Directed by Luc Jacquet.
movies|march-of-the-penguins.shortSynopsis: Emperor penguin parents get their chicks through an Antarctic winter, the males standing on the ice for two months without food.

movies|marriage-story.synopsis: A couple in New York are divorcing, and the film is about the lawyers, the mediator and the cost of it, told from both sides. Written and directed by Noah Baumbach, and the last two scenes are a monologue and a box of belongings.
movies|marriage-story.shortSynopsis: A New York couple's divorce, told from both sides, through lawyers, mediation and what is left at the end.

movies|master-and-commander.synopsis: An Royal Navy captain in 1805 commands a small ship that is outgunned and outnumbered, and his tactics win a fight that changes the war, and his leg is infected throughout it. Directed by Peter Weir, and the film is shot almost entirely in the cramped below-deck spaces of a ship.
movies|master-and-commander.shortSynopsis: An 1805 Royal Navy captain wins a sea fight that turns the war, with an infected leg throughout.

movies|matilda.synopsis: A girl at the end of primary school is a genius and nobody in her house can use it, and she is sent to a school where the headmistress is a tyrant, and the girl eventually deals with her. Adapted and directed by Danny DeVito, from Roald Dahl's book.
movies|matilda.shortSynopsis: A girl genius is sent to a school run by a tyrant, and deals with her before she has to be sent away.

movies|mean-girls.synopsis: A girl who has been raised by her father and only her father, is taught the rules of the school by a girl whose entire life is the rules, and the cost of it is the school. Directed by Mark Waters, and the film that made the word 'plastics' a term people use about their own friends.
movies|mean-girls.shortSynopsis: A girl raised by her father enters her new high school's caste system and is taught its rules by its queen.

movies|mean-streets.synopsis: A young man from Little Italy, a friend of Henry Hill who is twenty-four years old, gets involved in a protection racket after a dispute about a card game. Directed by Martin Scorsese, and the film is deliberately early, shot like a documentary, and released years before Goodfellas.
movies|mean-streets.shortSynopsis: A young man from Little Italy gets pulled into a protection racket after a dispute over a card game.

movies|meet-the-parents.synopsis: A man who works as a male nurse has to take his fiancée home to meet her father, who is a retired CIA operative and who has done background checks on the whole family, and who is not being hostile, he is being thorough. Directed by Jay Roach, and the film that made Robert De Niro a comic performer.
movies|meet-the-parents.shortSynopsis: A nurse takes his fiancée home to meet a retired CIA father who has investigated the whole family.

movies|memento.synopsis: A man who cannot form new memories is trying to work out who killed his wife, and has written tattoos on his body and taken Polaroids as reminders, and the film tells the story in reverse so the audience arrives at the beginning knowing the end. Written and directed by Christopher Nolan.
movies|memento.shortSynopsis: A man with anterograde amnesia investigates his wife's murder, in reverse order, with notes on his own body.

movies|midsommar.synopsis: A couple and a group of friends go to a Swedish midsummer for a wedding, and the things that are supposed to be harmless customs turn out to be a series of tests, and the film stops pretending anyone can leave. Written and directed by Ari Aster.
movies|midsommar.shortSynopsis: A group goes to a Swedish midsummer wedding, where the customs turn out to be a series of tests nobody can leave.

movies|millers-crossing.synopsis: A private investigator in 1946 Massachusetts is hired by a crime boss's son to get back a stolen diary, and both men want different things, and the son's girlfriend keeps changing her account. Written and directed by the Coen brothers, from a Dashiell Hammett novel.
movies|millers-crossing.shortSynopsis: A 1946 Massachusetts detective is hired to recover a diary by a crime boss's son who is not the client he seems.

movies|million-dollar-baby.synopsis: A boxing trainer's gym is shut down and he takes on a woman in her thirties who has never boxed, and trains her for a title fight, and the film's last twenty minutes is a question about what he owes her. Directed by Clint Eastwood, from a screenplay by Paul Haggis.
movies|million-dollar-baby.shortSynopsis: A trainer who has lost everything trains a woman for a title fight, and then has to answer for it.

movies|minority-report.synopsis: A police detective is arrested for a murder he did not commit in the twenty-first year, in a department that has stopped arresting people and started preventing them, and he goes looking for the one person who can overturn his case, and finds his own department. Directed by Steven Spielberg, from a Philip K. Dick short story.
movies|minority-report.shortSynopsis: A detective in a Precrime department is arrested for a murder he did not commit, and goes looking for the one person who can prove it.

movies|miracle.synopsis: The 1980 United States Olympic ice hockey team assembles in 1980, with a coach the players did not want, and wins the gold medal against a Soviet team that had won every game it entered for the previous two years. Directed by Gavin O'Connor.
movies|miracle.shortSynopsis: A US ice hockey team with a coach nobody wanted wins the 1980 Olympic gold against a Soviet team that had not lost.

movies|mirrormask.synopsis: A girl whose mother has been absent since she was small goes into a world behind a mirror, fights for a tress of hair belonging to a queen, and finds out what her own family has done. Written and directed by Dave McKean, with live action and a deliberately flat animation combined.
movies|mirrormask.shortSynopsis: A girl goes behind a mirror to recover a queen's hair, and finds out what her own family has done.

movies|misery.synopsis: A writer who has finished three novels about torture and is working on a fourth is driven to the mountains by a reader who has cared for him and now has him, and the question the film asks is about a book. Directed by Rob Reiner, from a Stephen King novel.
movies|misery.shortSynopsis: A writer of torture novels is driven to the mountains by a reader who has captured him.

movies|mission-impossible-fallout.synopsis: An agent has to steal the plans for a nuclear device from an Indian defector in Kashmir, and six months after he was thought dead he is not ready, and the last hour is a helicopter chase. Directed by Christopher McQuarrie, and the first Bond film written by the people who made the television series.
movies|mission-impossible-fallout.shortSynopsis: An agent has to steal nuclear plans from a defector in Kashmir, and is six months into a comeback he is not ready for.

movies|moana.synopsis: A wayfinder is chosen who has not sailed, and she wants to prove herself, and her brother is turned into an upholder of Te Fiti, which is what stops a plague of blight from a stolen heart, and the film is about who gives the heart back. Directed by Ron Clements and John Musker.
movies|moana.shortSynopsis: A wayfinder who has not sailed must return a stolen heart to a goddess, before her brother is needed at home.

movies|moneyball.synopsis: The Oakland Athletics' budget is a fraction of everyone else's, and their general manager decides to count things other than batting averages, and a young analyst arrives with a spreadsheet and no experience at all. Directed by Bennett Miller, from Michael Lewis's book, and the argument is about whether a season of wins matters.
movies|moneyball.shortSynopsis: The Oakland A's, outspent by everyone, hire a statistician who decides to count things other than batting average.

movies|monty-python-and-the-holy-grail.synopsis: A medieval comedy about a quest for the Holy Grail, told in scenes that end in a suicide and a castle and a rabbit, and built on a structure that was assembled around sketches rather than written as a story. Directed by Terry Gilliam, from a screenplay by the Python group.
movies|monty-python-and-the-holy-grail.shortSynopsis: A medieval quest for the Holy Grail, assembled from sketches rather than plotted, and ending in a castle.

movies|moonlight.synopsis: A boy in Miami is loved by two women, becomes a man who cannot be who either of them needs him to be, and then goes back, and the film is three chapters that do not connect by plot but by what they cost. Written and directed by Barry Jenkins, and the film that won Best Picture in 2017.
movies|moonlight.shortSynopsis: Three chapters on a boy in Miami and a man in Oakland, connected not by plot but by what each of them costs.

movies|moulin-rouge.synopsis: A writer who cannot write goes to a Paris cabaret to find a heroine he is not, and falls for a courtesan who has been bought by the Duke who wants the writer to stop writing about her. Directed by Baz Luhrmann, and filmed largely at night, in a building that was made of scaffolding.
movies|moulin-rouge.shortSynopsis: A writer falls for a Paris courtesan who has been bought by the man who does not want the story written.

movies|mrs-doubtfire.synopsis: A father loses his job and then loses a custody case and then decides to appear to his children as a woman, which works and which he cannot stop. Directed by Chris Columbus, and the film that established Robin Williams as somebody who could hold a serious subject and a joke at once.
movies|mrs-doubtfire.shortSynopsis: A father who loses a custody case appears to his children as a woman, and cannot stop appearing as one.

movies|murder-on-the-orient-express.synopsis: A murdered American's daughter and her companions are snowed in on a train crossing a continent, and a detective who has already been on two cases like this works out which of them did it. Directed by Kenneth Branagh, who also plays the detective, in a film made in 70mm.
movies|murder-on-the-orient-express.shortSynopsis: A detective works out which of eleven passengers killed a man on a train across a continent.

movies|my-fair-lady.synopsis: A cockney flower seller who is caught saying something the judge decides is an insult to his accent is given a year in a classroom to learn how to be a lady, and learns far more than he can teach her. Directed by George Cukor, and the film that made Audrey Hepburn and the song.
movies|my-fair-lady.shortSynopsis: A cockney flower seller is given a year to learn to be a lady, and teaches his professor more than he learns.

movies|my-neighbor-totoro.synopsis: Two sisters move to the country for their mother's illness, and the younger one makes a friend in the forest who is a large and silent and completely harmless creature. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, and the film that has no villain at all.
movies|my-neighbor-totoro.shortSynopsis: Two sisters move to the country, and the younger one befriends a large and silent forest creature.

movies|my-octopus-teacher.synopsis: A South African diver and a filmmaker are diving a kelp forest together during the kelp-baiting season, and one of them is stuck in a plastic bag and filmed being freed, and both say afterwards they have changed how they live. Co-directed by Pippa Ehrlich and James Reed, filmed on one camera.
movies|my-octopus-teacher.shortSynopsis: A South African diver and a filmmaker dive a kelp forest together, and one is caught in a plastic bag.

movies|mystic-river.synopsis: Three boys from a Boston housing project go to a marsh, and one of them does something to two of the others, and twenty-five years later two of them are on opposite sides of a murder investigation. Directed by Clint Eastwood, and the film that made it finally safe to read Dennis Lehane.
movies|mystic-river.shortSynopsis: Three boys from a Boston housing project go to a marsh, and one of them betrays the other two.

movies|napoleon-dynamite.synopsis: A nineteen-year-old in Preston, Idaho, has a crush on a girl in his trigonometry class, runs a small business selling things he has not got, and has to compete at a school exhibition against someone who has been cheating. Written and directed by Jared Hess, and shot on digital video for about twenty thousand dollars.
movies|napoleon-dynamite.shortSynopsis: A nineteen-year-old in Idaho has a crush, a business selling things he does not have, and a school exhibition to win.

movies|national-treasure.synopsis: A descendant of one of the men who wrote the Declaration of Independence reads a map hidden on the back of it and has a few days before it is auctioned, and the answer is a chamber somewhere in the country. Directed by Ron Howard, and the film is a chase that is really a list of national monuments.
movies|national-treasure.shortSynopsis: A descendant of a signer finds a map on the Declaration of Independence, and has days to find what it leads to.

movies|never-been-kissed.synopsis: A 1999 high school student is asked to be the school paper's yearbook queen, and a rival puts something in her drink to humiliate her, and he is not the one she expected. Directed by Drew Barrymore, in her directorial debut, and the phone and the press are a character.
movies|never-been-kissed.shortSynopsis: A high school girl is set up for a public humiliation by someone she trusted, and the school paper covers it.

movies|news-of-the-world.synopsis: In 1871 Texas, a man who makes his living reading the news in saloons is given a nine-year-old girl who has been living wild, and takes her across a country at war, and the film is about a man who has never had a child and is not sure he is allowed to keep her. Directed by Paul Greengrass, from a Paul Viragh novel.
movies|news-of-the-world.shortSynopsis: In 1871 Texas, a man who reads the news for a living takes a wild nine-year-old girl across a country at war.

movies|night-at-the-museum.synopsis: A museum where the exhibits come alive at night has a new night guard who is nobody's idea of qualified, and the displays are on a list of things to deal with before morning. Directed by Shawn Levy, and the film is the remake that worked.
movies|night-at-the-museum.shortSynopsis: A museum's exhibits come alive at night, and its new guard has to deal with them before morning.

movies|nightcrawler.synopsis: A man in Los Angeles with no money and no job discovers that photographs of a crime scene taken quickly can be sold to a news channel, and builds a business out of it, and the film follows him to a murder he arranged so he could photograph. Written and directed by Dan Gilroy, and Jake Gyllenhaal.
movies|nightcrawler.shortSynopsis: A broke man in Los Angeles finds that fast crime-scene photographs sell, and starts arranging the crimes.

movies|nims-island.synopsis: A girl raised on an island by her lighthouse-keeper father is told by a psychiatrist that he is right about everything, and leaves for Chicago to find out more, and there is a man there who has been waiting for her. Directed by Jim Strouse, and adapted from Danielewski's novel, with the island scenes shot on a real island.
movies|nims-island.shortSynopsis: A girl raised by her lighthouse-keeper father is told he is right, and leaves the island to find out why he waited so long.

movies|no-country-for-old-men.synopsis: A sheriff in west Texas finds a drug deal gone wrong with a great deal of money beside two dead men, and follows the money into a chase across the border, and the man he is chasing is not somebody a sheriff can chase. Written and directed by the Coen brothers, from a Cormac McCarthy novel.
movies|no-country-for-old-men.shortSynopsis: A Texas sheriff follows drug money across the border after a deal gone wrong, into a chase he is not equipped for.

movies|nomadland.synopsis: A woman is widowed, loses her job, and moves into a van, and the film follows her and other van-dwellers as they clean up national parks and refuse to stop. Directed by Chloé Zhao, and the non-actors in it are the van-dwellers themselves.
movies|nomadland.shortSynopsis: A woman is widowed, loses her job, moves into a van, and joins other van-dwellers cleaning national parks.

movies|north-by-northwest.synopsis: A New York advertising executive is mistaken for a secret agent, and is chased across the United States by men who are not going to stop, and the film's centrepiece is a night of mistaken identity involving a hotel. Directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and his most purely entertaining film.
movies|north-by-northwest.shortSynopsis: An advertising executive is mistaken for a secret agent and chased across America by people who will not stop.

movies|notting-hill.synopsis: A bookseller in Notting Hill falls in love with a famous American actress, and she comes down to his door, and the film is about the geography of a life and a street. Directed by Roger Michell, and the poster for it is the film's argument.
movies|notting-hill.shortSynopsis: A bookseller in Notting Hill falls in love with a famous actress, who comes down to his door.

movies|office-space.synopsis: A software engineer at a company that makes things a machine could have made is misdiagnosed, and begins a campaign of small acts of sabotage, and the film is about what happens when an organisation takes itself seriously. Written and directed by Mike Judge, from his own short film.
movies|office-space.shortSynopsis: A bored software engineer is misdiagnosed and begins a campaign of small acts of sabotage at his company.

movies|oldboy.synopsis: A man imprisoned for fifteen years without being told why, is released into a room with a television and a television is his, and a man comes and gives him the answer. Written and directed by Park Chan-wook, and the second part of a planned trilogy.
movies|oldboy.shortSynopsis: A man imprisoned for fifteen years without being told why is released, and a television is his only window.

movies|once.synopsis: An Irish busker and an Estonian piano player in Dublin meet for a week, and neither of them is looking for what they find, and the film is sung rather than scored. Written and directed by John Carney, and the film won the Oscar for Best Song.
movies|once.shortSynopsis: An Irish busker and an Estonian piano player meet in Dublin for a week, and neither was looking for it.

movies|once-upon-a-time-in-america.synopsis: A neighbourhood of Jewish families in Brooklyn, told through one boy who becomes a gangster, and the last shot is a red curtain in a theatre being used to hide a man. Directed by Martin Scorsese, and the last of his films about a group he grew up in.
movies|once-upon-a-time-in-america.shortSynopsis: A Brooklyn boy becomes a gangster among his own family, told across fifty years.

movies|once-upon-a-time-in-the-west.synopsis: A harmonica player is waiting for someone who has been a long time coming, and a land baron takes his land, and a bandit called the Colonel is working for both men. Directed by Sergio Leone, and the last film he completed.
movies|once-upon-a-time-in-the-west.shortSynopsis: A harmonica player waits in a station, while a land baron and a bandit work for each other.

movies|open-range.synopsis: In 1882 Wyoming, two cowboys who have had no fences and no trouble take a job driving cattle to a market, and the rancher they are taking them to has fences and a hired killer. Directed by Kevin Costner, who also directed his own script.
movies|open-range.shortSynopsis: Two free grazers in 1882 Wyoming take a cattle drive to a rancher who has fences and a killer.

movies|ordinary-people.synopsis: A family in a Chicago suburb is coming apart after the eldest son has killed himself, and the father tries to hold it together and the mother cannot, and the son who did it is the one who is well. Directed by Robert Redford, from a Judith Guest novel.
movies|ordinary-people.shortSynopsis: A Chicago family is coming apart after the eldest son killed himself, and the surviving son is the one who is well.

movies|paddington.synopsis: A small brown bear from 'darkest Peru' arrives in London in a lift with no button on the ground floor, and is taken in by a family, and there is a man in a basement who knows exactly what he is. Directed by Paul King, and a rare film that does not queue up two sequels in advance.
movies|paddington.shortSynopsis: A small brown bear arrives in London in a lift and is taken in by a family, and someone in a basement knows what he is.

movies|pans-labyrinth.synopsis: In 1944 Spain, a girl reading a book about a faun is told by the creature that he is the prince of a kingdom under the ground, and is given a task, and there is a captain in the house who is carving his name in the walls. Written and directed by Guillermo del Toro, and the story is set inside the book.
movies|pans-labyrinth.shortSynopsis: In 1944 Spain, a girl is told a faun is a prince, and given a task, while a captain carves his name in the walls beside her.

movies|parasite.synopsis: A family living in a semi-basement is employed, one by one, by a family living in a house above them, and the film keeps turning the house upside down as each of them is found out. Written and directed by Bong Joon-ho, and the first non-English film to win Best Picture.
movies|parasite.shortSynopsis: A family in a semi-basement is employed one by one by the family in the house above them.

movies|paths-of-glory.synopsis: French soldiers in 1916 are told to take a hill they cannot take, and are then told to hold one they cannot hold, and the film is about a colonel who understands something the general does not. Directed by Stanley Kubrick, from a novel by Humphrey Cobb.
movies|paths-of-glory.shortSynopsis: French soldiers in 1916 are ordered to take a hill they cannot take, then to hold one they cannot hold.

movies|patton.synopsis: A general who has been relieved and is now a commander in a place with no front, talks about how he intends to win the next war, and is put in hospital with a broken neck, and the film ends with a column of tanks going past him and a child asking who they are. Directed by Franklin J. Schaffner, and George C. Scott.
movies|patton.shortSynopsis: A relieved general in a place with no front talks about winning the next war, and a broken neck ends his career.

movies|peter-pan.synopsis: An animated film about a boy who will not grow up, who takes a girl to a place where she can be a child for ever, and who finds out that a pirate has been coming to the window for years. Directed by Clyde Geronimi, Wilfred Jackson and Hamilton Luske, and the film Disney returned to most seriously in 2003.
movies|peter-pan.shortSynopsis: A boy who will not grow up takes a girl to a place where she can be a child, and meets a pirate at the window.

movies|pirates-of-the-caribbean-the-curs.synopsis: A blacksmith is given a piece of the Aztec gold, which is stolen by a pirate who does not know what it is, and the two are pulled to an island where a curse is being broken. Directed by Gore Verbinski, and the first Pirates film, which made Depp's Jack Sparrow a character rather than a joke.
movies|pirates-of-the-caribbean-the-curs.shortSynopsis: A piece of Aztec gold draws a blacksmith, a pirate and a woman to a ship with a curse on it.

movies|platoon.synopsis: A nineteen-year-old is drafted into Vietnam and is handed to a sergeant who runs his platoon as a unit of predators, and then to a lieutenant who is worse, and the film does not say which of them was right. Directed by Oliver Stone, from his own service, and shot in a real rice paddy.
movies|platoon.shortSynopsis: A draftee in Vietnam is handed to a predatory sergeant and then a worse lieutenant, and the film does not say who was right.

movies|point-break.synopsis: An undercover officer in California is recruited into a group of bank robbers who surf, and is left on the mountain with a man who is the best at something in the world and would like to be left alone. Directed by Kathryn Bigelow, and the film that made the ending's shot a subject of analysis for thirty years.
movies|point-break.shortSynopsis: An undercover cop is recruited into a surfing bank-robbing crew and is left on a mountain with their best rider.

movies|poltergeist.synopsis: A family moves into a house where a television is apparently the thing making the noises, and moves out of it, and the son stays to find out who is behind it. Produced by Steven Spielberg and directed by Tobe Hooper, and the fight is with a television set.
movies|poltergeist.shortSynopsis: A house makes noise through its television, and a boy stays behind after his family has moved out to find out why.

movies|ponyo.synopsis: A girl on a sea cliff who cannot be introduced to the sea because of something her mother is afraid of meets a boy out of the water, and brings him home to her house, and the sea does not want him to stay. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, and the most openly autobiographical of his films.
movies|ponyo.shortSynopsis: A girl by the sea brings home a boy from the water, and the sea comes to get him back.

movies|predator.synopsis: A rescue team in Central America goes looking for a hostages and finds a set of skins, and something on the other side of them is stripping the jungle of anything it can build a trophy from, and the film is the first twenty minutes of something. Directed by John McTiernan.
movies|predator.shortSynopsis: A rescue team in Central America finds a set of stripped animal skins, and something is making them.

movies|pride-prejudice.synopsis: Elizabeth Bennet is sent to a house with an heir who has a large estate and a manner nobody can stand, and has to share a house with him, and the film ends with a proposal. Directed by Joe Wright, from Jane Austen's novel, and shot by the book rather than the adaptation.
movies|pride-prejudice.shortSynopsis: Elizabeth Bennet is made to share a house with the heir she has decided she cannot stand.

movies|princess-mononoke.synopsis: A young man takes a curse that will kill him slowly, and travels west to find out what is killing the forest gods, and there is an iron town and a wolf god who is angry, and the god of the forest is being poisoned by human industry. Written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, and the first film to beat Disney at the Oscars.
movies|princess-mononoke.shortSynopsis: A man carrying a curse travels west to find what is poisoning the forest gods, and finds an iron town.

movies|prisoners.synopsis: Two girls go missing in a Pennsylvania town, and a detective works the case outside the law because his own daughter was taken from him. Directed by Denis Villeneuve, and the film is about two men who will not stop and cannot say why.
movies|prisoners.shortSynopsis: Two girls go missing in Pennsylvania, and a detective works the case outside the law because of his own daughter.

movies|psycho.synopsis: A secretary takes money from her boss and drives somewhere with it, and stops at a motel run by a young man and his mother, and the film tells the audience about the shower in advance. Directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and the last film in which he controlled the production himself.
movies|psycho.shortSynopsis: A secretary with stolen money stops at a motel, in the film that told us about the shower in advance.

movies|public-enemies.synopsis: The FBI hunts John Dillinger in 1933 and 1934 with a man from Kansas who has never shot anyone, who is allowed to, because the Bureau wants it done. Directed by Michael Mann, and the film is about the head of the Bureau and the man he uses to work.
movies|public-enemies.shortSynopsis: The FBI hunts John Dillinger with a Kansas agent allowed to shoot because the Bureau needs it done.

movies|pulp-fiction.synopsis: Two hitmen, a boxer who should not take the fight, a gangster's wife and a pair of diner criminals who decide to rob it. The stories do not meet until the end, where two of them do not know each other and have a conversation. Written and directed by Quentin Tarantino.
movies|pulp-fiction.shortSynopsis: Two hitmen, a boxer who should not fight, a gangster's wife and two diner robbers, whose stories meet at the end.

movies|puss-in-boots-the-last-wish.synopsis: Puss has used up one of his nine lives, which has to be spoken of because the last time it was forgotten a great deal went wrong, and he wants to be a horse again, and to stop being a cat. Directed by Joel Crawford, and the second film.
movies|puss-in-boots-the-last-wish.shortSynopsis: Puss has used up one of his nine lives and wants to be a horse, and to stop being a cat.

movies|raging-bull.synopsis: A middleweight boxer in the Bronx fights his way out of a childhood of being beaten by his father, and is beaten by the men he beats, and retires to a job ringing bells. Directed by Martin Scorsese, from a memoir, and filmed in black and white where it needs to be.
movies|raging-bull.shortSynopsis: A Bronx boxer fights his way out of a childhood of being beaten, and retires to ringing bells.

movies|raiders-of-the-lost-ark.synopsis: An archaeologist is hired by the American army to find the Ark, which the Nazis are also looking for, and the film has a boulder, a truck and a submarine in it. Directed by Steven Spielberg, and the film that made the adventure sequence a set-piece vocabulary.
movies|raiders-of-the-lost-ark.shortSynopsis: An archaeologist races the Nazis to the Ark, with a boulder, a truck and a submarine.

movies|rambo-first-blood.synopsis: A Vietnam veteran is taken through a mountain town by six police officers on their way to deliver him to the local jail, and he takes the town apart to get back. Directed by Ted Kotcheff, and the film that made Stallone's character a sympathetic man.
movies|rambo-first-blood.shortSynopsis: A Vietnam veteran takes a small town apart to get back to it, having been driven through it by six police officers.

movies|ratatouille.synopsis: A rat in Paris can cook, and works in the kitchen of a restaurant he cannot be seen in, and the chef who is a nobody there is the one with the food, and neither of them knows what the other is. Written and directed by Brad Lewis, and the Pixar film about the relationship between food and the person cooking it.
movies|ratatouille.shortSynopsis: A rat who can cook works in a restaurant kitchen he cannot be seen in, for a chef who is a nobody.

movies|rbg.synopsis: A documentary about Ruth Bader Ginsburg, built from interviews, home video and the arguments she has made in court, including the ones she did not win. Directed by Mimi Leder, and the film is about a person who kept not winning and did not stop.
movies|rbg.shortSynopsis: A documentary about Ruth Bader Ginsburg, including the arguments she made in court and did not win.

movies|ready-player-one.synopsis: In a 2040s where everyone is in a virtual world, a young man is searching for an easter egg that leads to a prize nobody has claimed, and the people after him are not going to stop. Directed by Steven Spielberg, from Ernest Cline's novel, and the references are the point.
movies|ready-player-one.shortSynopsis: In a 2040s virtual world, a young man searches for an easter egg that leads to a prize nobody has claimed.

movies|rear-window.synopsis: A photographer with a broken leg watches a courtyard across the way with binoculars, and works out that one of the neighbours has killed his wife, and the last act of the film is somebody falling off a building. Directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and the film that made the audience a camera.
movies|rear-window.shortSynopsis: A photographer with a broken leg watches a courtyard and works out that a neighbour has killed his wife.

movies|rebecca.synopsis: A woman goes to Monte Carlo as a companion to a widow, and stays in a hotel with a reputation, and is given a room that belonged to somebody else, and slowly works out whose. Directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and the only film Alfred directed that won Best Picture.
movies|rebecca.shortSynopsis: A woman at a hotel with a reputation is given a room that belonged to somebody else.

movies|remember-the-titans.synopsis: A high school in Alexandria, Virginia, ends a fifty-year record of football failure by importing a new coach who moves in with the black players, and the story is about the town rather than the team. Directed by Boaz Yakin, from a book by Alan Shanks.
movies|remember-the-titans.shortSynopsis: A failing Virginia high school hires a coach who moves in with his black players, and a town tries to cope.

movies|rent.synopsis: Eight people in the East Village in the 1990s share an apartment, and one of them has AIDS, and the film is a year of their lives. Directed by Chris Columbus, from Jonathan Larson's stage musical, which was about eight people in the East Village in the 1990s and which he wrote in a coffee shop on Avenue A.
movies|rent.shortSynopsis: Eight people share an apartment in the East Village, and one of them has AIDS, and it is a year of their lives.

movies|requiem-for-a-dream.synopsis: Four people on Caddo Lane in Coney Island take different routes into the same thing, and the film is shot to feel like the inside of their heads, and the last twenty minutes are shot in continuous two-minute takes. Directed by Darren Aronofsky, and the film won Best Cinematography.
movies|requiem-for-a-dream.shortSynopsis: Four people on Caddo Lane take different routes into addiction, shot to feel like the inside of their heads.

movies|reservoir-dogs.synopsis: A diamond heist goes wrong, and the surviving members of the group are in a warehouse arguing about which of them did it, and the film goes back to show what happened an hour earlier. Written and directed by Quentin Tarantino, and the torture scene is short and its length is the point.
movies|reservoir-dogs.shortSynopsis: A diamond heist goes wrong and the survivors argue in a warehouse about which of them did it.

movies|rio-bravo.synopsis: A sheriff refuses to let a prisoner be transferred, because the man who is coming to collect him is the man who killed the sheriff's brother. Directed by Howard Hawks, and the film is about four people in a room and two outside it.
movies|rio-bravo.shortSynopsis: A sheriff keeps a dangerous prisoner in his jail, because the man collecting him killed his brother.

movies|robocop.synopsis: A Detroit police officer rebuilt as a machine after being killed, is not told what he is, and the corporation that did it wants him back as a product, and the city has a problem with the parts of him that were still a man. Directed by Paul Verhoeven, and the film that made ED-209 a signature.
movies|robocop.shortSynopsis: A Detroit cop rebuilt as a machine is not told what he is, and the corporation wants him back as a product.

movies|rocky.synopsis: A thirty-year-old money collector in Philadelphia who trains in a basement takes an exhibition fight against a heavyweight in order to keep his job and his girlfriend, and goes the full distance. Directed by John G. Avildsen, and the film's budget was under a million dollars.
movies|rocky.shortSynopsis: A Philadelphia money collector trains for an exhibition fight with a heavyweight to keep his job and his girlfriend.

movies|rocky-iv.synopsis: A Philadelphia boxer is invited to fight a Soviet champion who killed his friend, and he is forty and out of shape, and the film is a training montage cut against a man who has everything. Directed by Sylvester Stallone, the fourth of the series.
movies|rocky-iv.shortSynopsis: A Philadelphia boxer is invited to fight a Soviet champion who killed his friend, and is forty and out of shape.

movies|roman-holiday.synopsis: A princess of a small European state is bored, and a day is arranged for her, and she gets out of the car and does not come back, and there is a reporter on the same day. Directed by William Wyler, and the film that won Audrey Hepburn an Oscar she was too shy to collect in person.
movies|roman-holiday.shortSynopsis: A bored princess spends a day in Rome without her schedule, and a reporter spends it following her.

movies|romancing-the-stone.synopsis: A woman who writes bestselling romance novels is sent by her editor to find a stolen diamond in a jungle temple, and is followed by two men who want it, one of whom is her brother. Directed by Ronald Zimmer, and the film that turned Kathleen Turner into a physical performer and established the template for Indiana Jones and every film that followed it.
movies|romancing-the-stone.shortSynopsis: A romance novelist is sent to find a stolen diamond in a jungle temple, followed by her brother and his best friend.

movies|room.synopsis: A woman and her five-year-old son are held in a locked room for seven years, and the film's structure is the first half from inside the room and the second half from outside it. Directed by Lenny Abrahamson, adapted from Emma Donoghue's novel.
movies|room.shortSynopsis: A woman and her son are held in a locked room for seven years, told from inside and then from outside.

movies|rosemarys-baby.synopsis: A young couple move into a famous building and are befriended by an elderly neighbour who is, with her husband and a group of people around her, part of a Satanic cult, and the couple are given a role in a plan. Directed by Roman Polanski, and the film that made the title sound ordinary.
movies|rosemarys-baby.shortSynopsis: A young couple move into a famous building and are drawn into a Satanic cult's plan for a baby.

movies|rudy.synopsis: A man who could not get into Notre Dame football as a young man is small and comes from a family of six brothers, and takes a job at the university grounds, and is eventually let onto the team as a walk-on. Directed by David Anspaugh, from a Daniel Ruettiger memoir.
movies|rudy.shortSynopsis: A small man from a family of brothers who could not get into Notre Dame finally gets onto the team at thirty.

movies|saving-private-ryan.synopsis: Eight soldiers are sent behind enemy lines to find a paratrooper whose three brothers have all been killed, and the beach is twenty-seven minutes long. Directed by Steven Spielberg, and the first twenty-six minutes of it was shot on the Duxford runway with the camera at waist height.
movies|saving-private-ryan.shortSynopsis: Eight soldiers go behind enemy lines to find a paratrooper whose three brothers have all been killed.

movies|saw.synopsis: A man wakes in a locked room with a corpse, a phone, a video and a set of instructions, and the film is the first of a series in which the trap is the plot. Written by Leigh Whannell and directed by James Wan, who also had the same idea and did not tell Whannell.
movies|saw.shortSynopsis: A man wakes in a locked room with a corpse, a video and instructions, and has to make one painful choice.

movies|scarface.synopsis: A Cuban refugee arrives in Miami and works his way up the cocaine trade by the only method available, which is to be worse than everybody, and the film follows him as his supplier and his money are the same person. Written by Oliver Stone, directed by Brian De Palma.
movies|scarface.shortSynopsis: A Cuban refugee takes over the Miami cocaine trade by being worse than everybody already in it.
