games|monster-hunter-world.shortSynopsis: You track monsters by footprint, and the tracking is a real mechanic. Capcom, 2018.

games|monument-valley.synopsis: A game of impossible architecture in which you rotate the world to make a path, and it is beautiful enough that the puzzle is optional. ustwo, 2014.
games|monument-valley.shortSynopsis: Impossible architecture you rotate to make a path. ustwo, 2014, and beautiful enough to skip the puzzle.

games|mortal-kombat-1.synopsis: A reboot of a fighting game that spent decades being extremely unpleasant, in which this one is deliberately grotesque and the story is a horror film. NetherRealm, 2021.
games|mortal-kombat-1.shortSynopsis: A deliberately grotesque reboot of a series that was extremely unpleasant. 2021.

games|mortal-kombat-11.synopsis: The entry in which the series stopped being a set of finishing moves and became a story about a tournament and a man trying to leave it. NetherRealm, 2019.
games|mortal-kombat-11.shortSynopsis: The entry where the series became a story about a man trying to leave a tournament. 2019.

games|motogp-23.synopsis: The official motorcycle road racing game, in which the braking is the game and the licence is most of the product. Milestone, 2022.
games|motogp-23.shortSynopsis: Official MotoGP, where the braking is the game and the licence is the product. 2022.

games|move-or-die.synopsis: A game in which you must be doing something in order to survive, and the idle state kills you, and it is a game about anxiety designed as a joke. Those Awesome Guys, 2016.
games|move-or-die.shortSynopsis: Standing still kills you, and it is anxiety designed as a joke. Those Awesome Guys, 2016.

games|moving-out.synopsis: A game in which you and up to three other people move a house, and the objects are furniture and the tools are the wrong shape for the job. System Era Softworks, 2020.
games|moving-out.shortSynopsis: Moving a house with other people, and the tools are the wrong shape. 2020.

games|multiversus.synopsis: A platform fighter built on Warner Bros' library, launched with a roster of six and released free, and the game's whole business case was in the roster. LightSpeed Studios, 2022.
games|multiversus.shortSynopsis: A platform fighter on a Warner Bros library, launched with six characters. 2022.

games|muse-dash.synopsis: A rhythm game where you hold one button to hit everything and that is the entire control scheme, and the difficulty is in choosing a character. PeroPeroGames, 2016.
games|muse-dash.shortSynopsis: One button hits everything, and the difficulty is picking a character. PeroPeroGames, 2016.

games|muv-luv.synopsis: A visual novel in which the first third is a comedy about an academy and the other two thirds are a war, and the tonal switch is the point and is unforgiving. âge, 2003.
games|muv-luv.shortSynopsis: A school comedy for a third, then a war, and the switch is the point. âge, 2003.

games|my-time-at-portia.synopsis: A life simulation in which you inherit your father's workshop in a town that is rebuilding after a war, and the game is about the fact that everyone there has the same problem. Pathea Games, 2019.
games|my-time-at-portia.shortSynopsis: You inherit a workshop in a town rebuilding after a war, and everyone has the same problem. 2019.

games|naraka-bladepoint.synopsis: A melee-focused battle royale in which the game is entirely about reading another person's three moves, and it is a competitive game. 24 Entertainment, 2021.
games|naraka-bladepoint.shortSynopsis: A melee battle royale that is entirely about reading three moves. 24 Entertainment, 2021.

games|nba-2k23.synopsis: The annual basketball simulation, in which the difference between editions is a roster and the game underneath is a genuine attempt at the sport. Visual Concepts, 2022.
games|nba-2k23.shortSynopsis: The annual basketball sim, and a genuine attempt at the sport underneath. 2022.

games|nba-2k24.synopsis: The same game as nba-2k23, a year later, with a different roster, held as a separate row because the series is versioned by year. Same game, later release.
games|nba-2k24.shortSynopsis: The same game as nba-2k23, a year later. A duplicate row.

games|need-for-speed-heat.synopsis: A street racing game in which the police chase is a gradual escalation rather than a chase, and the game is about the week and the heat building across it. Ghost Games and EA, 2018.
games|need-for-speed-heat.shortSynopsis: A gradual police escalation rather than a chase, built across a week. EA, 2018.

games|need-for-speed-most-wanted.synopsis: The 2005 open world street racing game, in which the street is a list of drivers and the game is about working down it, and it is the one the series is judged against. EA Black Box, 2005.
games|need-for-speed-most-wanted.shortSynopsis: The 2005 open world racer, and the one the series is judged against. 2005.

games|nekopara.synopsis: A game about a boy who inherits a cafe staffed by catgirls, where the business is failing and the food is bad, and the game is about the cooking and about work. NEKO WORKs, 2017, and the visual novel and the eroge are the same work.
games|nekopara.shortSynopsis: A boy inherits a failing cafe staffed by catgirls, and the game is the cooking. 2017.

games|neverwinter-nights.synopsis: A role-playing game set in a city-state under siege, in which the game's most consequential decision is at the start, where you have to break a siege or the world ends. BioWare, 2002.
games|neverwinter-nights.shortSynopsis: A siege of a city-state, and the most consequential decision is at the start. BioWare, 2002.

games|nhl-24.synopsis: The annual ice hockey game, in which the difference between editions is a licence and the simulation underneath has been in development for two decades. EA, 2023.
games|nhl-24.shortSynopsis: The annual ice hockey game, on a two-decade-old simulation. EA, 2023.

games|nickelodeon-all-star-brawl.synopsis: A licensed platform fighter in which the roster is four Nickelodeon channels, and it was free and good and everybody assumed it would last. Ludosity and Fair Play Labs, 2021.
games|nickelodeon-all-star-brawl.shortSynopsis: A free, good licensed platform fighter on a Nickelodeon roster. 2021.

games|nidhogg.synopsis: A fighting game in which the match is over after two seconds and the game is entirely about the frames, and it is the only game in which the loser is whoever reacts first. Message Box, 2014.
games|nidhogg.shortSynopsis: A fighter decided in two frames, and the loser reacts first. Message Box, 2014.

games|nier-automata.synopsis: An action role-playing game in which the world is largely empty because everything has been done to it, and the story is a question asked twice with different answers. PlatinumGames, 2017.
games|nier-automata.shortSynopsis: An empty world, and a question asked twice with different answers. PlatinumGames, 2017.

games|ninja-gaiden.synopsis: A 1988 action game in which you are a ninja who cannot jump and the game is a series of very long rooms, and it is the origin of the wall. Tecmo, 1988, and the series was remade in 2004.
games|ninja-gaiden.shortSynopsis: A ninja who cannot jump, in very long rooms. Tecmo, 1988.

games|nioh.synopsis: An action role-playing game in which you die constantly and losing gear is a real possibility, and the setting is Sengoku Japan with the oni from the record attached. Team Ninja, 2015.
games|nioh.shortSynopsis: Sengoku Japan with the oni from the record attached, and losing gear is real. 2015.

games|nioh-2.synopsis: The sequel, in which the setting is Edo rather than Sengoku and the game is about firearms and about a town. Team Ninja, 2020.
games|nioh-2.shortSynopsis: The sequel, set in Edo, about firearms and about a town. 2020.

games|no-mans-sky.synopsis: A game on a galaxy of procedurally named planets in which the first version launched unfinished and the second was the same game with the promises kept. Hello Games, 2016 and 2018.
games|no-mans-sky.shortSynopsis: A galaxy of procedurally named planets, released unfinished and then finished. 2016, 2018.

games|northgard.synopsis: A strategy game about building a village in a Norse winter in which the antagonist is the climate, and it is a small game with a large amount of care in it. Shiro Games, 2017.
games|northgard.shortSynopsis: A Norse village where the antagonist is the climate. Shiro, 2017.

games|octopath-traveler.synopsis: A role-playing game with eight characters and a deliberately opaque system, in which the game is about the stories and the systems are a barrier in front of them. Square Enix, 2018.
games|octopath-traveler.shortSynopsis: Eight characters and opaque systems, where the game is the stories. Square Enix, 2018.

games|one-finger-death-punch.synopsis: A game in which one button and one finger is the entire control scheme, and the difficulty is that the whole thing is happening while you are trying to look casual. Mike Klubnika, 2014.
games|one-finger-death-punch.shortSynopsis: One button, one finger, and you have to look casual doing it. 2014.

games|one-piece-pirate-warriors.synopsis: A licensed action game in which several hundred manga characters fight each other, and it is a very good action game that nobody pretends is a story. Omega Force, 2020.
games|one-piece-pirate-warriors.shortSynopsis: Several hundred manga characters fighting, and a very good action game. 2020.

games|ooblets.synopsis: A creature-collecting game in which the creatures are also your farm labour and also a barter economy, and there is no battle system, which upset people. Glumberland, 2020.
games|ooblets.shortSynopsis: Creature collecting where the creatures farm, and there is no battle system. 2020.

games|ori-and-the-blind-forest.synopsis: A platform game about a small white creature in a forest at night, and the art is the argument and the game underneath is real. Moon Studios, 2015.
games|ori-and-the-blind-forest.shortSynopsis: A small white creature in a forest at night, and a real game underneath. 2015.

games|ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.synopsis: The sequel, which splits the narrative between a tree and a creature and adds combat that the first game did not have. Moon Studios, 2020.
games|ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.shortSynopsis: The sequel, splitting the story between a tree and a creature, and adding combat. 2020.

games|osu.synopsis: A rhythm game with no content at all, where the content is other people's songs and the difficulty is generated from how you play. Australian bean, 2007, and free.
games|osu.shortSynopsis: A rhythm game with no content, where the content is other people's songs. 2007, free.

games|outer-wilds.synopsis: A game in which the only thing that is not a loop is your knowledge, and the ending is an ending and not a boss. Mobius Digital, 2019, and the only game in this list I would argue is the best of.
games|outer-wilds.shortSynopsis: The only thing that is not a loop is your knowledge. Mobius, 2019.

games|outlast.synopsis: A survival horror game in which you are a journalist and the camera is the only weapon you have, which means the game is about a machine that is documenting you. Red Barrels, 2013.
games|outlast.shortSynopsis: A camera is the only weapon, and the game is about being documented. 2013.

games|outlast-2.synopsis: The sequel, which is about a cult rather than an asylum and which spends its first hour deliberately making you hate the character. Red Barrels, 2017.
games|outlast-2.shortSynopsis: A cult rather than an asylum, and an hour spent making you hate the lead. 2017.

games|outward.synopsis: A survival game in which your shelter, your equipment and your own body are all damaged, and the second half is a game about a man who cannot be helped. Obsidian Entertainment, 2019.
games|outward.shortSynopsis: Your shelter, your gear and your body are all damaged, and it is about being unhelped. 2019.

games|overcooked.synopsis: A game in which you prepare and serve food in a kitchen that is too small, with other people, and the difficulty is entirely about communication. Ghost Town Games, 2017.
games|overcooked.shortSynopsis: Too small a kitchen, other people, and the difficulty is communication. 2017.

games|overcooked-2.synopsis: The sequel, which adds boats, a swinging platform and a time machine, and none of which is better than the first game. Ghost Town Games, 2019.
games|overcooked-2.shortSynopsis: Boats, swinging platforms and a time machine, none better than the first. 2019.

games|overwatch.synopsis: A team shooter in which the characters do not shoot each other, and the game is a composition of six abilities moving around an objective, and it is a genre that has not produced much since. Blizzard, 2016.
games|overwatch.shortSynopsis: A team shooter where characters do not shoot each other, and the game is composition. 2016.

games|overwatch-2.synopsis: The sequel, in which the game moved to five a side, added open areas and a battle pass, and the review consensus was that it got worse in the ways that matter. Blizzard, 2022.
games|overwatch-2.shortSynopsis: Five a side, open areas, a battle pass, and it got worse. 2022.

games|star-wars-jedi-survivor.shortSynopsis: Traversal and survival with a stilt, and combat is the least of it. 2023.

comics|giant-days.synopsis: A 2013 comics anthology for teenagers in which nothing is filtered and the awkwardness is real, which is what the format usually gets wrong. Aimee Friedman, 2013.
comics|giant-days.shortSynopsis: A teen anthology where nothing is filtered and the awkwardness is real. 2013.

comics|gideon-falls.synopsis: A 2014 comic in which a man in a hospital bed receives messages predicting murders, and the mystery is whether he is reliable. Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino, 2014.
comics|gideon-falls.shortSynopsis: A man in a bed receiving murder predictions, and whether to trust them. 2014.

comics|girl-genius.synopsis: A webcomic from 2002 in which a mad scientist is trying to build a boy and has built the same one repeatedly by accident, and the world is full of people who will kill her for it. Phil and Kaja Foglio, from 2002.
comics|girl-genius.shortSynopsis: A mad scientist who keeps building the same boy by accident. From 2002.

comics|girls-of-the-wilds.synopsis: A 2020 comic about two girls from a hard place who are good at something specific and bad at everything else, and the book is about what they do with that. From 2020.
comics|girls-of-the-wilds.shortSynopsis: Two girls good at one thing and bad at everything else. 2020.

comics|girls-with-slingshots.synopsis: A 2004 webcomic about four friends in their twenties having conversations that could be about anything, and the strip is almost entirely text, and it is the reason any webcomic works in this register. Keystone, from 2004.
comics|girls-with-slingshots.shortSynopsis: Four friends in their twenties, almost entirely text, conversations. 2004.

comics|god-of-bath.synopsis: A 2006 webcomic in which a man is cursed to live in a bathroom and the strip is about the design problem, and it is funnier than that sentence. From 2006.
comics|god-of-bath.shortSynopsis: A man cursed to live in a bathroom, and the design problem. 2006.

comics|golden-kamuy.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2014, and it is a thriller about a treasure hunt run by a man with a tattoo on his skin. Satoru Noda, from 2014.
comics|golden-kamuy.shortSynopsis: A treasure hunt run by a man with a tattoo on his skin. 2014.

comics|gotham-central.synopsis: A 2002 series in which the story is told entirely by the police, about a city that is at the end of a long bad year, and it is a detective comic that takes the detective out. Greg Rucka, 2002.
comics|gotham-central.shortSynopsis: Gotham told by the police, with the detective removed. Rucka, 2002.

comics|gotham-underground.synopsis: A 1997 series in which the city is at the end of a long bad year and the people who live there have had years to get used to it, and the police are the compromise. Dennis O'Neil, 1997.
comics|gotham-underground.shortSynopsis: A city at the end of a long bad year, and the police are the compromise. 1997.

comics|grass.synopsis: A 1992 comic in which a family in a suburban cul-de-sac has a monster living behind the fence, and the monster is not the frightening part. Jeff Mason, 1992.
comics|grass.shortSynopsis: A monster behind the fence of a suburban house, and it is not the frightening part. 1992.

comics|green-arrow.synopsis: A 2011 run in which the character is a man who was an idiot before he was a hero, and the book is about the class he came from. Geoff Johns, 2011.
comics|green-arrow.shortSynopsis: A hero who was an idiot first, and the class he came from. Johns, 2011.

comics|green-lantern.synopsis: A 2011 run in which the character is a man chosen by a ring, and the run is the best superhero science fiction comic of its decade. Geoff Johns, 2011.
comics|green-lantern.shortSynopsis: A man chosen by a ring, and the best superhero science fiction of its decade. 2011.

comics|groo-the-wanderer.synopsis: A 1980s barbarian comic in which the character is the worst person alive and the jokes depend on the reader knowing that. Steve Grogg, 1982.
comics|groo-the-wanderer.shortSynopsis: A barbarian who is the worst person alive, and the jokes know it. 1982.

comics|guardians-of-the-galaxy.synopsis: A 2013 run that took five throwaway cosmic characters and made them the best-written team in the company. Brian Michael Bendis, 2013.
comics|guardians-of-the-galaxy.shortSynopsis: Five throwaway cosmic characters made into the best team in the company. 2013.

comics|gunnerkrigg-court.synopsis: A 2005 webcomic in which a girl at a school with a science and a magic department, and the science side is where the story is, and Tom Siddell drew the magic in 3D. From 2005.
comics|gunnerkrigg-court.shortSynopsis: A school with a science and a magic department, and the science wins. 2005.

comics|habibi.synopsis: A 2010 graphic novel set in an invented version of the medieval Islamic world with no magic in it at all, and the density of research is visible on every page. Craig Thompson, 2010.
comics|habibi.shortSynopsis: A medieval Islamic world with no magic and visible research. Thompson, 2010.

comics|hard-boiled.synopsis: A 1990 comic in which a detective in a city with no name is also the worst person in the book, and it is the most accurate crime comic about what the work does to you. David Lapham, 1990.
comics|hard-boiled.shortSynopsis: A detective who is the worst person in the book. Lapham, 1990.

comics|hardcore-leveling-warrior.synopsis: A 2020 webtoon in which a man gets the worst possible power-up and commits to it with a straight face, and the art is extraordinary. Jee-Gyu Kim and Yeon Hyeok, 2020.
comics|hardcore-leveling-warrior.shortSynopsis: The worst possible power-up, committed to with a straight face. 2020.

comics|hark-a-vagrant.synopsis: A 2014 webcomic in which a woman who is a disaster is handed a sword and a mission, and the banter is the actual plot. Kate Beaton, from 2014.
comics|hark-a-vagrant.shortSynopsis: A disaster of a woman handed a sword, and the banter is the plot. 2014.

comics|harrow-county.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which a young woman returns to a town in a state built entirely on one resource, and the horror is documentary. Ethan Young and Tyler Stash, 2016.
comics|harrow-county.shortSynopsis: A town built on one resource, and the horror is documentary. 2016.

comics|head-lopper.synopsis: A 2014 comic in which a man whose head has been removed from his body hunts the man who did it, and the art is a black-and-white lithograph look. Benjamin Percy and Erica Guidel, 2014.
comics|head-lopper.shortSynopsis: A headless man hunting the man who removed his head. 2014.

comics|heartstopper.synopsis: A 2017 graphic novel in which two boys work out that they like each other in a series of conversations, and it is better written than almost anything with a plot. Alice Oseman, 2017.
comics|heartstopper.shortSynopsis: Two boys working out they like each other, in conversations. 2017.

comics|heartstopper-vol-2.synopsis: The second volume of the series above, in which the relationship survives contact with other people, and it is better than the first. Alice Oseman, 2019.
comics|heartstopper-vol-2.shortSynopsis: The second volume, where the relationship meets other people. 2019.

comics|heavy-metal.synopsis: A 1977 adult illustrated magazine that funded animated science fiction films nobody else would, and its art direction alone justifies the existence of the American magazine. From 1977.
comics|heavy-metal.shortSynopsis: A 1977 adult magazine that funded animated science fiction nobody else would.

comics|hellblazer.synopsis: A 1988 DC series in which the hero is a man who sells his soul, does it again, and sells it back, and the book is about the gap between the man and the arrangement. Garth Ennis, 1988.
comics|hellblazer.shortSynopsis: A man selling his soul repeatedly, and the gap between man and arrangement. 1988.

comics|hellboy.synopsis: A 1994 comic in which the hero is a man raised by a Nazi Wizard in an unfamiliar shape, and the books are about institutions rather than fights. Mike Mignola, 1994.
comics|hellboy.shortSynopsis: A man raised by a Nazi Wizard, and the books are about institutions. 1994.

comics|hellboy-odd-jobs.synopsis: The framing volume of the series above, in which the character recounts the jobs he has had to other versions of himself, and the framing is better than the content. Mignola, 2005.
comics|hellboy-odd-jobs.shortSynopsis: The framing volume, told to other versions of himself. Mignola, 2005.

comics|hellboy-seed-of-destruction.synopsis: The 1994 origin in which the character is still the wrong shape and a Nazi Wizard is trying to fix him, and the horror of the first books is not in them. Mignola, 1994.
comics|hellboy-seed-of-destruction.shortSynopsis: The 1994 origin, wrong shape, a Nazi Wizard trying to fix it. 1994.

comics|homestuck.synopsis: A 2009 webcomic that used page length as a variable and then spent a chapter not drawing at all, and the community analysis of it is now a larger genre than the comic. Andrew Hussie, from 2009.
comics|homestuck.shortSynopsis: A webcomic that made page length and silence into a device. 2009.

comics|hopalong-cassidy.synopsis: A 1907 newspaper strip in which the hero does not speak, the villains are recognisable from across the page, and the art is the best thing in early comics. Harold Gray, 1907.
comics|hopalong-cassidy.shortSynopsis: A silent hero, villains visible from across the page. Gray, 1907.

comics|house-of-mystery.synopsis: A 2005 DC series in which a man inherits a house that is bigger on the inside and the book is about what the previous owners did in it. James Robinson, 2005.
comics|house-of-mystery.shortSynopsis: A house bigger on the inside and what its last owners did. 2005.

comics|house-of-secrets.synopsis: A 1996 DC series in which a man who has spent his life in a house on a hill is the villain, and the book is a real political argument. James Robinson, 1996.
comics|house-of-secrets.shortSynopsis: A man who stayed in his house becoming the villain. Robinson, 1996.

comics|hunter-x-hunter.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 1998, and the first arc is a shonen manga and the rest is something else. Yoshihiro Togashi, from 1998.
comics|hunter-x-hunter.shortSynopsis: A shonen first arc and then something else entirely. Togashi, from 1998.

comics|hyperbole-and-a-half.synopsis: A 2009 webcomic in which everything is drawn badly on purpose, and the autobiographical material in it is the thing that made it famous. Allie Brosh, 2009.
comics|hyperbole-and-a-half.shortSynopsis: Everything drawn badly on purpose, and the autobiography is why. 2009.

comics|incognito.synopsis: A 2008 series in which the world's greatest supervillain is put under a spell that makes him an alter ego and has to be a good person, and the book is about a bad person doing paperwork. Brian K Vaughan, 2008.
comics|incognito.shortSynopsis: A supervillain made good, and a bad person doing paperwork. 2008.

comics|invincible.synopsis: A 2003 comic in which the world's strongest man has an ordinary Tuesday, and the series' argument is that the world would be like that if he existed and you did not need it. Robert Kirkman, Cory Walker, Ryan Ottley, 2003.
comics|invincible.shortSynopsis: The strongest man having an ordinary Tuesday. Kirkman, 2003.

comics|iron-man.synopsis: A 2012 Marvel run in which a man who is unambiguously awful is allowed to be the protagonist, and the run is better for not pretending otherwise. David Slapy and Kieron Gillen, 2012.
comics|iron-man.shortSynopsis: A man who is unambiguously awful allowed to be the protagonist. 2012.

comics|iron-man-war-machine.synopsis: A 2015 Marvel run in which the two characters are forced to share a suit and take turns, and the book is about two men who cannot stand each other. AFK, 2015.
comics|iron-man-war-machine.shortSynopsis: Two rivals forced to share a suit and take turns. 2015.

comics|its-a-bird.synopsis: A 2020 comic in which a boy goes to find the superhero who disappeared, and the hero has been a bird, and the investigation is the book. Stephen McCauley and Jared Goldstein, 2020.
comics|its-a-bird.shortSynopsis: A boy searching for a missing hero who has been a bird. 2020.

comics|jimmy-corrigan-the-smartest-kid-o.synopsis: A 2017 graphic novel in which a child comic genius is too small to do anything about the problems he identifies, and the book is about that specific frustration. Written by Greta Gerwig, illustrated by Charlie Adlard, 2017.
comics|jimmy-corrigan-the-smartest-kid-o.shortSynopsis: A child genius too small to act on what he knows. Gerwig, 2017.

comics|jinx.synopsis: A 2013 series about a woman who gets what she asks for and the book is the cost. From 2013.
comics|jinx.shortSynopsis: A woman who gets what she asks for, and the cost. 2013.

comics|jojos-bizarre-adventure.synopsis: A 1987 manga in which each part is set in a different decade and a different country with a different art style, and the menace is a creature that is somehow more frightening as a friendly man. Hirohiko Araki, from 1987.
comics|jojos-bizarre-adventure.shortSynopsis: A manga that changes decade, country and art style every part. 1987.

comics|jonah-hex.synopsis: A 2007 DC western in which the character is a man cursed to raise the dead and cannot stop, and it is a revenge story that keeps going past the revenge. Justin Gray and Jody Houser, 2007.
comics|jonah-hex.shortSynopsis: A cursed man who cannot stop raising the dead, past the revenge. 2007.

comics|journey-into-mohawk-country.synopsis: A 2017 graphic novel in which a teenager living in a New York housing project is told by his father to get out and finds the Hudson Valley, and the book is about who gets to live where. Richard Sala, 2017.
comics|journey-into-mohawk-country.shortSynopsis: A teenager sent out of a housing project, and who owns what. 2017.

comics|judge-dredd.synopsis: A 1977 character in which the law is absolute, the sentence is instant, and the character's job is to be the thing that does not need a trial. 2000 AD, 1977.
comics|judge-dredd.shortSynopsis: Instant judgement, no trial, and the character enforces it. 1977.

comics|jujutsu-kaisen.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2018, and the premise is a boy who swallows a finger. Gege Akutami, from 2018.
comics|jujutsu-kaisen.shortSynopsis: A boy who swallows a finger. The original, 2018.

comics|junji-itos-cat-diary.synopsis: A 2018 manga in which two girls keep a diary addressed to their cats, and the horror is a wall of detail at a scale nobody else works at. Junji Ito, 2018.
comics|junji-itos-cat-diary.shortSynopsis: A diary addressed to their cats, and horror at a vast scale. 2018.

comics|justice-league.synopsis: A 2013 DC run in which the team is the least remarkable thing in the books and the arguments are about the state of the world. Geoff Johns, 2013.
comics|justice-league.shortSynopsis: The team is the least remarkable thing, and the arguments are the book. 2013.

comics|kill-or-be-killed.synopsis: A 2014 Image series in which a woman discovers she is a superhero and that the hero work is a contract, and the book is about the contract. Robert Kirkman, John Burns, Ethan Moore, 2014.
comics|kill-or-be-killed.shortSynopsis: A woman who is a hero, and the hero work is a contract. 2014.

comics|kill-six-billion-demons.synopsis: A 2015 webcomic in which the world is being ended by a war on an epic scale and the protagonists are a priest and a bartender, and it is a dungeon crawl drawn in an early-2000s style. Chris Sebela, 2015.
comics|kill-six-billion-demons.shortSynopsis: A priest and a bartender in a war ending the world, drawn in 2000s style. 2015.

comics|kingdom-come.synopsis: A 1996 DC graphic novel illustrated entirely in photorealism, in which a future without superheroes arrives and the man who watched the whole history is old, and it predicted nearly all of it. Alex Ross, 1996.
comics|kingdom-come.shortSynopsis: A future without superheroes, illustrated in photorealism. Ross, 1996.

comics|kramers-ergot.synopsis: A 2006 webcomic in which a man in a cube office is given a press, and the whole thing is about an idea not surviving contact with making it. Roman Klimentov, 2006.
comics|kramers-ergot.shortSynopsis: A cube office, a press, and an idea failing in production. 2006.

comics|krazy-kat.synopsis: A 1913 strip in which a cat, a policeman and a love story are all one, the artist drew the war in it as it was happening, and the letters are from real people. George Herriman, 1913.
comics|krazy-kat.shortSynopsis: A cat, a policeman and a love story, with the war as it happened. 1913.

comics|kubera.synopsis: A 2004 Dark Horse comic in which an unknowable being exists in every land and a narrator tries to describe it and fails in a different way each time. From 2004.
comics|kubera.shortSynopsis: An unknowable being, described differently and failing each time. 2004.

comics|lazarus.synopsis: A 2013 science fiction comic in which a company owns a person and there is a race of people bred for it, and Greg Rucka is writing a real thriller. Greg Rucka and Michael Lark, 2013.
comics|lazarus.shortSynopsis: A company that owns a person and breeds for it. Rucka, 2013.

comics|least-i-could-do.synopsis: A 2012 webcomic in which a man wakes up as a skeleton in the world of a game and treats the situation as a job, and the world design is genuinely hostile. Ryan Sohmer, 2012.
comics|least-i-could-do.shortSynopsis: A man who wakes as a skeleton in a game world, treated as a job. 2012.

comics|legend-of-the-northern-blade.synopsis: A 2018 webtoon in which an immortal is betrayed, retires to the mountains, and raises an army, and the drawing is the reason it is a thousand pages. From 2018.
comics|legend-of-the-northern-blade.shortSynopsis: A betrayed immortal raising an army in the mountains. 2018.

comics|lil-abner.synopsis: A 1934 newspaper strip set in a town full of people who are not clever and are entirely certain of themselves, and its lexicon entered the language. Al Capp, 1934.
comics|lil-abner.shortSynopsis: A town of certain, not clever people, and its own lexicon. 1934.

comics|little-nemo-in-slumberland.synopsis: A 2006 comic in which a company that owns the character tries to use him, and the book is about what happens to the dream when it is owned. Bill Willingham, 2006.
comics|little-nemo-in-slumberland.shortSynopsis: What happens to the dream when the character is owned. 2006.

comics|locke-key.synopsis: A 2008 comic in which a family of keys can open anything, including doors that should not exist, and the father is not telling them why. Joe Hill and Gabriel Rodriguez, 2008.
comics|locke-key.shortSynopsis: A family of keys that open anything, and an unexplained father. 2008.

comics|long-way-down.synopsis: A 2018 graphic novel in which a boy gets on a lift to kill someone and tells himself a poem on the way up, and the poem is the structure. Jonah Winter, 2018.
comics|long-way-down.shortSynopsis: A boy on a lift to kill someone, telling himself a poem. 2018.

comics|lookism.synopsis: A 2014 webtoon in which one person with two bodies is the premise, and the argument about it is the most interesting thing in Korean webtoons. Park Tae-jun, 2014.
comics|lookism.shortSynopsis: One person with two bodies, and the argument is the point. 2014.

comics|love-and-rockets.synopsis: A 1984 comics anthology in which a set of characters run a shop and the stories are about work and relationships and nothing happens, and it was the first book like this. Howard Cruse, 1984.
comics|love-and-rockets.shortSynopsis: People running a shop, and nothing happens, and it was the first. 1984.

comics|loveless.synopsis: A 2018 graphic novel in which a girl is assigned a dominant female and a submissive male as a treatment and becomes neither, and the book is about consent as a plot device. Loish, 2018.
comics|loveless.shortSynopsis: A treatment that assigns roles, and becoming neither. Loish, 2018.

comics|luann.synopsis: A 1989 strip in which a sixteen-year-old has a mother who draws her as a cartoon, and the two are the joke. Greg Evans, 1989.
comics|luann.shortSynopsis: A teenager whose mother draws her as a cartoon. Evans, 1989.

comics|lucifer.synopsis: A 2004 DC series in which God is alive, running a nightclub, and does not get on with his son, and the premise is funny and then it is not. Mike Carey, 2004.
comics|lucifer.shortSynopsis: God alive and running a nightclub, and not getting on with his son. 2004.

comics|lucky-luke.synopsis: A 1946 Franco-Belgian western comic whose hero shoots faster than anyone can draw and the joke is that he is stupid about everything else. Morris, 1946.
comics|lucky-luke.shortSynopsis: The fastest draw in comics, and stupid about everything else. 1946.

comics|lumberjanes.synopsis: A 2014 comic about a summer camp for girls who fight monsters, and the books are about the friendship rather than the monsters. Noelle Stevenson, 2014.
comics|lumberjanes.shortSynopsis: A summer camp for girls who fight monsters, and it is about friendship. 2014.

comics|mad-magazine.synopsis: A 1952 magazine that satirised everything and had a real, functioning editorial process, and its art department is the reason a generation of artists went into comics. From 1952.
comics|mad-magazine.shortSynopsis: A 1952 satirist magazine whose art department trained a generation. 1952.

comics|made-in-abyss.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2012, and the horror is that the deepest places are more interesting than the surface. Akihito Tsukushi, 2012.
comics|made-in-abyss.shortSynopsis: Horror about what the deepest places want. The original, 2012.

comics|manifest-destiny.synopsis: A 2009 series in which six armed convicts are shot out of a prison ship as a controlled experiment, and the argument is about whether they are people. Brian K Vaughan, 2009.
comics|manifest-destiny.shortSynopsis: Six convicts shot out of a ship as an experiment, on purpose. 2009.

comics|march.synopsis: A 2013 graphic novel in which John Lewis retells the civil rights movement as a first-person narrative, and it is unusually honest about the parts that did not work. From 2013.
comics|march.shortSynopsis: The civil rights movement retold first-person, and honestly. 2013.

comics|marvel-comics-presents.synopsis: A 1968 Marvel title that was four issues of a different book plus an unrelated lead, and it is where Spider-Man's popularity is visible as a publishing decision. Marvel, 1968.
comics|marvel-comics-presents.shortSynopsis: A 1968 title that existed to publish a comic nobody else would. 1968.

comics|maus.synopsis: A 1986 graphic novel in which the author's parents are drawn as cats and mice according to what they were, and the whole book is a man trying to get his father to talk about it. Art Spiegelman, 1986.
comics|maus.shortSynopsis: The author's parents as cats and mice, and a man trying to get a story. 1986.

comics|mind-mgmt.synopsis: A 2012 comic in which a woman wakes up and someone else is operating her, and the book is about consent and about the FBI. Matt Kindt, 2012.
comics|mind-mgmt.shortSynopsis: A woman whose body is being operated by someone else. 2012.

comics|monster.synopsis: A 1997 manga in which a doctor commits the perfect crime to save someone and then spends the rest of the book watching it not work, and the artwork is the best in comics. Naoki Urasawa, from 1997.
comics|monster.shortSynopsis: A perfect crime committed to save someone, watched for years not working. 1997.

comics|little-nemo-anthology.synopsis: A 1905 newspaper strip in which a boy goes somewhere impossible every Sunday, the new world is always the reward for going to sleep, and Winsor McCay drew things no one else drew. From 1905.
comics|little-nemo-anthology.shortSynopsis: A boy who goes somewhere impossible every Sunday. McCay, 1905.

comics|hagar-the-horrible.synopsis: A 1973 newspaper strip in which a Viking is cheerfully terrible and his enemies are a Roman centurion and a Lapp, and the humour is that nobody in it knows they are in a joke. Dik Browne, 1973.
comics|hagar-the-horrible.shortSynopsis: A cheerfully terrible Viking, his Roman enemy, and nobody knows it's a joke. 1973.

comics|haikyuu.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2006, and the premise is a very short boy on a very tall team. Haruichi Furudate, from 2006.
comics|haikyuu.shortSynopsis: A very short boy on a very tall volleyball team. Furudate, 2006.

comics|here.synopsis: A 1993 comic that takes a single room and one conversation between a man and a woman and never leaves the room, and it is the best demonstration of what the form can do that nobody has attempted since. Roberto Rusch, 1993.
comics|here.shortSynopsis: One room, one conversation, and never leaving it. 1993.

comics|hi-fructose.synopsis: A 2004 alt-weekly comic in which nothing supernatural happens and the two characters simply do not understand each other, and the strip is about that. Shadi Petosky, from 2004.
comics|hi-fructose.shortSynopsis: Nothing supernatural, two people who do not understand each other. 2004.

comics|home-sick-pilots.synopsis: A 2013 webcomic in which a pilot and a passenger in a small aircraft are stuck together and it is almost entirely about the conversation, and the situation is the joke. Ben_operand, from 2013.
comics|home-sick-pilots.shortSynopsis: A pilot and a passenger stuck in a small aircraft, talking. 2013.

comics|honor-girl.synopsis: A 2003 autobiographical comic in which a comic artist's week is a series of small professional indignities, and the dignity in the title is the joke. Peter Bagge, 2003.
comics|honor-girl.shortSynopsis: A comic artist's week of small professional indignities. Bagge, 2003.

comics|ice-cream-man.synopsis: A 1996 series in which the neighbourhood ice cream man turns out to be the most reliable person in the city, and the stories are about the city's need for one. Waid and Kolka, 1996.
comics|ice-cream-man.shortSynopsis: The ice cream man as the most reliable person in the city. 1996.

comics|in-real-life.synopsis: A 2009 webcomic in which real situations are drawn without a punchline, and the strip is about how absurd ordinary interactions are. From 2009.
comics|in-real-life.shortSynopsis: Ordinary interactions drawn absurd, with no punchline. 2009.

comics|kari.synopsis: A 2007 webcomic in which a woman who is not good at being a person tries to get better at it, and the joke is that there is no better at it. From 2007.
comics|kari.shortSynopsis: A woman not good at being a person, getting better at it. 2007.

comics|kid-colt-outlaw.synopsis: A 1949 Dell western in which the hero is a gunman with a heart condition, and the stories are about how little time he has. From 1949.
comics|kid-colt-outlaw.shortSynopsis: A 1949 western hero with a heart condition. Dell.

comics|monstress.synopsis: A 2015 comic in which a war is fought by people who are monstrous, arranged as a school, and the book refuses to say the war is the point. Lyslexia, from 2015.
comics|monstress.shortSynopsis: A war fought by monsters, arranged as a school. 2015.

comics|moon-knight.synopsis: A 2011 Marvel run in which the character is a man with a dissociative identity disorder and a costume, and the book is about the illness being the mechanism. From 2011.
comics|moon-knight.shortSynopsis: A hero whose dissociative disorder is the mechanism. Marvel, 2011.

comics|ms-marvel.synopsis: A 2014 Marvel run in which a Muslim woman from Jersey who does not want the costume is given it, and the book is about not wanting it. G. Willow Wilson, 2014.
comics|ms-marvel.shortSynopsis: A Muslim woman from Jersey who does not want the costume. 2014.

comics|mutt-and-jeff.synopsis: A 1914 newspaper strip in which a tennis player and his valet are both stupid in different ways, and it ran for fifty years without changing the formula. Bud Fisher, 1914.
comics|mutt-and-jeff.shortSynopsis: A tennis player and his valet, both stupid differently. Fisher, 1914.

comics|my-hero-academia.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2014, and the premise is a world where everyone has a power and the interesting one has no power at all. Kohei Horikoshi, 2014.
comics|my-hero-academia.shortSynopsis: A world where everyone has a power and one boy has none. 2014.

comics|nailbiter.synopsis: A 2014 webcomic in which a girl in a school where everyone is a celebrity has a completely ordinary life, and the whole thing is written as a confession. Noelle Stevenson, 2014.
comics|nailbiter.shortSynopsis: An ordinary girl at a school of celebrities, written as a confession. 2014.

comics|negative-burn.synopsis: A 1993 anthology in which a person is on fire, and the imagery is held for the whole run, and the stories are about what it is like to be the one it is happening to. Scott Snyder and Joe Pruett, 1993.

comics|the-beginning-after-the-end.synopsis: A 2013 web novel and webtoon in which a man reincarnates into a world where cultivating is real and the world is more racist than his own, and he has to work with that. Tapas, 2013.
comics|the-beginning-after-the-end.shortSynopsis: Reincarnated into a cultivation world, which is more racist. 2013.

comics|the-black-hood.synopsis: A 2012 Archie comic in which the character is a masked crimefighter who is a veteran, and the book is the gap between the costume and the person. Duemaine, 2012.
comics|the-black-hood.shortSynopsis: A veteran in a mask, and the gap to the person. 2012.

comics|the-boxer.synopsis: A 2014 graphic novel about two brothers in an unnamed country who are the best fighters in it, and the country is the point. Gene Luen Yang, 2014.
comics|the-boxer.shortSynopsis: Two brothers who are the best fighters in their country. 2014.

comics|the-boys.synopsis: A 2006 comic in which a superhero team is watched by a man whose job is to keep them in line, and the book is about the paperwork. Garth Ennis and Darick Robertson, 2006.
comics|the-boys.shortSynopsis: A hero team watched by a man whose job is the paperwork. 2006.

comics|the-buffalo-hunter.synopsis: A 2010 comic in which a man tracks an animal across a wilderness and the wilderness is a character, and the book is about the tracking. Jason Hardwick, 2010.
comics|the-buffalo-hunter.shortSynopsis: A man tracking an animal, and the wilderness as a character. 2010.

comics|hack-slash.synopsis: A 2010 comic in which a warrior kills monsters for hire and the party is assembled by an advertising agency, and the horror is on the business side. Tim Seeley, 2010.
comics|hack-slash.shortSynopsis: Monster hunters assembled by an advertising agency. 2010.

comics|gunhawks.synopsis: A 1988 comic in which two bounty hunters on opposite sides keep missing each other in space, and it is drawn as though the film version were being shot. Timothy Truman, 1988.
comics|gunhawks.shortSynopsis: Two bounty hunters on opposite sides, missing each other. 1988.

comics|peerless-dad.synopsis: A 2012 graphic novel in which a father at home alone with three children is a genuine disaster, and the drawing is the same style as his other books. Jeff Smith, 2012.
comics|peerless-dad.shortSynopsis: A father home alone with three children, a genuine disaster. 2012.

comics|second-life-ranker.synopsis: A 2019 comic in which the last person left in a world is a bored office worker who works his way up a ranking system nobody else is using, and the book is about that. 2019..
comics|second-life-ranker.shortSynopsis: The last person in a world, climbing a ranking nobody uses. 2019.

comics|sisters.synopsis: A 2021 McSweeney's comic anthology in which a writer and her sister talk about a woman who drowned, and they are both doing it. Charles Paul Wilson III, 2021.
comics|sisters.shortSynopsis: Two sisters talking about a woman who drowned. 2021.

comics|sgt-rock.synopsis: A 1970 DC war comic in which the character refuses to stop fighting, and the run's reputation is that the editors kept sending him back in. Joe Kubert, 1970.
comics|sgt-rock.shortSynopsis: A soldier who refuses to stop fighting. Kubert, 1970.

comics|sinfest.synopsis: A 2000 webcomic in which the world is hell and the character's philosophical despair is genuinely funny, and the strip is about small cruelties. Kris Wilson, 2000.
comics|sinfest.shortSynopsis: A world that is hell, and small cruelties. 2000.

comics|all-star-western.synopsis: A 1970 DC western in which the character's origin is retold, including the parts of it that do not work, and the book is about a genre correcting its own record. From 1970.
comics|all-star-western.shortSynopsis: A 1970 western retelling its own origin, including the bad parts. 1970.

comics|american-cowboy.synopsis: A 1970 European western comic in which the character is a cowboy who is a coward who is genuinely good at his job, and the jokes come from the gap. Charlier and Morris, 1970.
comics|american-cowboy.shortSynopsis: A coward who is genuinely good at being a cowboy. 1970.

comics|flight.synopsis: A 2004 graphic anthology in which a steampunk inventor's life is told in fragments by a different artist in every story, and the fragmentation is the design. Kazu Kibuishi, 2004.
comics|flight.shortSynopsis: A steampunk life told in fragments by a different artist each time. 2004.

comics|lore-olympus.synopsis: A 2017 comic in which the Greek gods are modern and exhausted and the man telling it is immortal and bored, and the world is drawn as a corporate filing. Ryan North, 2017.
comics|lore-olympus.shortSynopsis: Greek gods as modern and exhausted, drawn as a corporate filing. 2017.

comics|nano-machine.synopsis: A 2019 webtoon in which a man is injected with a machine that can rebuild a body, and the book is about what he does with the money. Mat Rudy, 2019.
comics|nano-machine.shortSynopsis: A machine that rebuilds a body, and what he does with it. 2019.

comics|point-blank.synopsis: A 2019 comic in which an assassin working for the state is sent after one man and then stops, and the book is about the stopping. Oclair, 2019.
comics|point-blank.shortSynopsis: A state assassin who stops. Oclair, 2019.

comics|queen-country.synopsis: A 2010 graphic novel in which a violent man wants to be the queen of a small town, and the book is written as a romance and read as a threat. 2010.
comics|queen-country.shortSynopsis: A violent man wants to be queen of a small town. 2010.

comics|scalped.synopsis: A 2008 comic in which a sheriff in a Native American reservation is systematically killing people, and the book is the investigation told as the crime. Kurt Busiek, 2008.
comics|scalped.shortSynopsis: A sheriff killing people on a reservation, told as the investigation. 2008.

comics|snapdragon.synopsis: A 2020 webtoon in which a man who cannot die and cannot leave his village has been doing the same five jobs forever, and the book is about a phone call. Ryu Fujisaki, 2020.
comics|snapdragon.shortSynopsis: A man who cannot die or leave his village, and a phone call. 2020.

comics|special-forces.synopsis: A 2011 comic in which two soldiers from opposite wars in the same country fight together, and the book's subject is that they are the same. David Axe, 2011.
comics|special-forces.shortSynopsis: Two soldiers from opposite wars in one country, and they are the same. 2011.

comics|solo-dc-anthology.synopsis: A 2004 DC one-shot in which each story is drawn by a different artist, and the book is a good survey of how many styles the company had in one year. DC, 2004.
comics|solo-dc-anthology.shortSynopsis: One artist per story, and a survey of the company's styles. 2004.

comics|spx-anthology.synopsis: A 2015 Image anthology in which the stories are from a very wide range of creators with no theme connecting them, and the range is the point. Image, 2015.
comics|spx-anthology.shortSynopsis: No connecting theme, a very wide range of creators. 2015.

comics|star-trek-the-next-generation.synopsis: A 1994 comic in which the series is drawn in the outlined style of the original show, which everyone in comics considered a mistake and which is the only reason to read it. IDW, 1994.
comics|star-trek-the-next-generation.shortSynopsis: Drawn in the show's outlined style, which was considered a mistake. 1994.

comics|terry-and-the-pirates.synopsis: A 2014 comic reboot in which the pulp serial is reset with Terry in the modern day, and the same plot beats happen anyway, and the book is about that. From 2014.
comics|terry-and-the-pirates.shortSynopsis: A pulp serial rebooted into the present, hitting the same beats. 2014.

comics|the-complete-maus.synopsis: The collected edition of the memoir above, and the reason the graphic novel is taught in schools, and the two-slice process survives the enlargement. Art Spiegelman, 1986 and 1991.
comics|the-complete-maus.shortSynopsis: The collected Maus, and the reason it is taught in schools. 1986 and 1991.

comics|the-complete-peanuts.synopsis: The collected newspaper strip above, in a reprint that was delayed for years by rights, and the delay is itself a small history of comics publishing. From 1950.
comics|the-complete-peanuts.shortSynopsis: The collected Peanuts, delayed for years by rights. From 1950.

comics|the-dark-knight-returns.synopsis: A 1986 comic in which an old Batman comes back and the world is worse, and the book is about what the character's success was for. Frank Miller, 1986.
comics|the-dark-knight-returns.shortSynopsis: An old Batman returns to a worse world. Miller, 1986.

comics|the-empty-man.synopsis: A 2018 comic in which a man is infected with something that takes his body but leaves him alive in it, and the horror is that the process is pleasant. From 2018.
comics|the-empty-man.shortSynopsis: A man whose body is taken from him pleasantly. 2018.

comics|the-fade-out.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which people are losing the ability to concentrate, and the book is about what happens to a society that stops paying attention. Scott Snyder and Charles Soule, 2016.
comics|the-fade-out.shortSynopsis: A society losing the ability to concentrate. 2016.

comics|the-far-side.synopsis: A 1980 newspaper strip in which nothing in the world makes sense and that is never explained, and the accuracy of the animals is what makes the jokes work. Gary Larson, 1980.
comics|the-far-side.shortSynopsis: A world where nothing makes sense, and it is never explained. 1980.

comics|the-far-side-strip.synopsis: The same strip as the row above, held separately because the importer split the title on a format qualifier. Same work.

comics|the-flash.synopsis: A 2009 DC run in which the character is a scientist who can move so fast he cannot hold anything, and the book is about the cost of that, written slowly. Geoff Johns, 2009.
comics|the-flash.shortSynopsis: A man who is too fast to hold anything. Johns, 2009.

comics|the-girl-who-would-be-king.synopsis: A 2012 comic in which a man and a woman train to be king and the training is the book and the tournament at the end is a formality. Mike Norton, 2012.
comics|the-girl-who-would-be-king.shortSynopsis: A man and a woman training to be king, and the training. 2012.

comics|the-god-of-high-school.synopsis: A 2010 webtoon in which a man comes back from the dead to beat up high school students, and it is a genuinely serious book about a broken country wearing a fighting comic. Park Tae-jun, 2010.
comics|the-god-of-high-school.shortSynopsis: A man returns from the dead to beat up students, seriously meant. 2010.

comics|the-immortal-hulk.synopsis: A 2010 Marvel series in which a man cannot die or heal and the book is about being unable to get worse, which is a different horror. Paul Jenkins, 2010.
comics|the-immortal-hulk.shortSynopsis: A man who cannot die or heal, and that is worse. 2010.

comics|the-man-with-no-name.synopsis: A 2014 comic sequel to the character, in which the western is in a future where the whole genre is a historical memory, and the film role is adapted as written. Dynamite, 2014.
comics|the-man-with-no-name.shortSynopsis: A sequel to the western, set in a future that remembers it. 2014.

comics|the-manhattan-projects.synopsis: A 2011 comic in which the scientists who built the atomic bomb are given the same treatment as superhero villains, and the book asks whether that is accurate. Jonathan Hickman, 2011.
comics|the-manhattan-projects.shortSynopsis: The atom bomb scientists as supervillains, and whether that is fair. 2011.

comics|the-meek.synopsis: A 2012 comic in which the samurai is a coward who is very good at fighting, and every drawing of him is worse than the last. Derf Backderf, 2012.
comics|the-meek.shortSynopsis: A coward who is very good at fighting. Backderf, 2012.

comics|the-metabarons.synopsis: A 1999 comic in which a family of warriors across centuries are each someone's child, and the book's structure is a family tree drawn as a family tree. Alejandro Jodorowsky and Moebius, 1999.
comics|the-metabarons.shortSynopsis: A family of warriors across centuries, drawn as a family tree. 1999.

comics|the-nam.synopsis: A 1987 comic in which a single soldier is followed through the Vietnam war, and the character's face is never fully shown, and the book is about that. Archie Goodwin and Jim Shooter, 1987.
comics|the-nam.shortSynopsis: One soldier through the Vietnam war, never fully shown. 1987.

comics|the-nao-of-brown.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which a boy and a whale are friends and the whale is a person, and the book is about a relationship across a category. Abby Howard, 2016.
comics|the-nao-of-brown.shortSynopsis: A boy and a whale who are friends, across a category. 2016.

comics|the-nib.synopsis: A 2010 webcomic in which two rival writers argue about whether comics matter, in a format that is mostly that argument. From 2010.
comics|the-nib.shortSynopsis: Two writers arguing about whether comics matter. 2010.

comics|the-oatmeal.synopsis: A 2009 webcomic in which everyday annoyances are turned into epic narratives, and the format is a single comic per complaint. Matthew Inman, 2009.
comics|the-oatmeal.shortSynopsis: Everyday annoyances turned into epic narratives. 2009.

comics|the-october-faction.synopsis: A 2007 comic in which a man who talks to the dead is recruited by a side that wants them dead, and the joke and the horror are the same thing. Steven Grant, 2007.
comics|the-october-faction.shortSynopsis: A man who talks to the dead, recruited by one side. 2007.

comics|the-perry-bible-fellowship.synopsis: A 2001 webcomic about amateur theatre in which the productions are always terrible and the people are completely sincere, and that is the whole book. Nick Derington, 2001.
comics|the-perry-bible-fellowship.shortSynopsis: Amateur theatre, always terrible, always sincere. 2001.

comics|the-photographer.synopsis: A 2012 graphic novel in which a war photographer photographs a war, and the second half of the book is photographs of a real trip the author took. Emmanuel Guibert, 2009.
comics|the-photographer.shortSynopsis: A war photographer, then photographs of a real trip. Guibert, 2009.

comics|the-photographer-literary.synopsis: The same graphic novel as the row above, held separately because the importer split the title on a genre qualifier. Same work.
comics|the-photographer-literary.shortSynopsis: The same graphic novel as the-photographer, split on a genre qualifier. A duplicate row.

comics|the-plot.synopsis: A 2001 comic in which a masked vigilante in a corrupt city is systematically undermined, and the book's title is a joke about how comics are made. Graham McNeill and Michael Allred, 2001.
comics|the-plot.shortSynopsis: A masked vigilante in a corrupt city, undermined on schedule. 2001.

comics|the-realm.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which the fantasy world is reached through a series of increasingly unpleasant practical realities, and the door is always more mundane than the world. From 2016.
comics|the-realm.shortSynopsis: A fantasy world reached through unpleasant mundane doors. 2016.

comics|the-rocketeer.synopsis: A 1939 comic in which the character is a pilot who is also a Nazi in a costume and the books played it for the adventure, and Dave Stevens made it literal. From 1939.
comics|the-rocketeer.shortSynopsis: A pilot who is a Nazi in a costume. Stevens, from 1939.

comics|the-sandman.synopsis: A 1989 series in which the characters are the embodiments of things and the main one is the Dream, and the books gave comics a plot to be about that lasted thirty years. Neil Gaiman, 1989.
comics|the-sandman.shortSynopsis: The embodiments of things, and it gave comics a plot. 1989.

comics|the-sixth-gun.synopsis: A 2007 comic in which six objects are the only weapons that can kill a particular kind of monster, and six people are looking for them, and the book is about the looking. Scott Snyder and Nick Derington, 2007.
comics|the-sixth-gun.shortSynopsis: Six weapons and six people looking for them. 2007.

comics|the-sixth-gun-days-of-the-dead.synopsis: The sequel to the series above, in which the world has ended, and the difference in tone between the two is the point. Scott Snyder, 2013.
comics|the-sixth-gun-days-of-the-dead.shortSynopsis: The sequel, after the world ends, in a different tone. 2013.

comics|the-tick.synopsis: A 1992 comic in which the hero is a large man in a suit who fights a lesser-known villain because there is no other book for him, and the book is about a character who is a placeholder. Ben Edlund, 1992.
comics|the-tick.shortSynopsis: A hero who exists because there is no book for anyone else. 1992.

comics|the-unwritten.synopsis: A 2009 comic in which the main character is a character inside a comic who knows he is one, and the series is about a story looking for its author. Mike Carey and Peter Gross, 2009.
comics|the-unwritten.shortSynopsis: A character who knows he is one, and a story looking for its author. 2009.

comics|the-vault-of-horror.synopsis: A 2019 Image comic in which five people inherit a house whose owners keep things in the walls, and the book is the inspection. From 2019.
comics|the-vault-of-horror.shortSynopsis: Five people inheriting a house with things in the walls. 2019.

comics|the-walking-dead.synopsis: A 2003 comic in which the dead come back and the series is about a group of ordinary people who keep being bad at this, and it is the reason a cable network made a drama. Robert Kirkman, 2003.
comics|the-walking-dead.shortSynopsis: The dead come back and a group of people are bad at coping. 2003.

comics|the-white-donkey.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which a soldier is sent back to the battlefield after the war, repeatedly, and the book is about the deployment itself. From 2016.
comics|the-white-donkey.shortSynopsis: A soldier sent back to a finished war, and the deployment. 2016.

comics|the-wicked-the-divine.synopsis: A 2016 comic in which the gods are pop stars and the book is about what happens when they are famous. Kieron Gillen and Emma Ríos, 2016.
comics|the-wicked-the-divine.shortSynopsis: The gods as pop stars, and what fame does to them. 2016.

comics|the-witcher.synopsis: A 1998 comic in which a man who takes contracts on monsters tells the story of one in particular, and the books understand that the work is ordinary. From 1998.
comics|the-witcher.shortSynopsis: A man who takes contracts on monsters, and one in particular. 1998.

comics|the-wizard-of-id.synopsis: A 1964 newspaper strip in which three barbarians and a wizard are all stupid in a castle, and the wizard's catchphrases are the whole show. Terry Jones, 1964.
comics|the-wizard-of-id.shortSynopsis: Three barbarians and a fool wizard in a castle. 1964.

comics|the-yellow-kid.synopsis: A 1896 newspaper comic in which the character is a child in rags drawn in a yellow shirt so newspapers could print him cheaply, and the invention is the character's entire function. Richard Outcault, 1896.
comics|the-yellow-kid.shortSynopsis: A child in a yellow shirt so papers could print him cheaply. 1896.

comics|this-one-summer.synopsis: A 2009 graphic novel in which two men have one summer in a seaside town and it goes wrong, and the characters are named for their first names throughout. Guy Delisle, 2009.
comics|this-one-summer.shortSynopsis: Two men, one summer in a seaside town, going wrong. 2009.

comics|thor.synopsis: A 2014 Marvel run in which the character is a god being tested by people who do not believe in him, and the book is about a claim nobody will accept. Jason Aaron, 2014.
comics|thor.shortSynopsis: A god tested by people who do not believe in him. 2014.

comics|through-the-woods.synopsis: A 2018 comic in which three girls in a small French village are certain something is wrong and are right, and the book is about being believed. From 2018.
comics|through-the-woods.shortSynopsis: Three girls certain something is wrong, and being believed. 2018.

comics|tokyo-ghoul.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2011, and a college student is turned into one of the things he studied. Sui Ishida, 2011.
comics|tokyo-ghoul.shortSynopsis: A student turned into the thing he studied. Ishida, 2011.

comics|tomie.synopsis: A 2005 manga in which a woman is murdered repeatedly by different people in different stories and she keeps coming back and nobody is permanently satisfied, and that structure is the book. Junji Ito, 2005.
comics|tomie.shortSynopsis: A woman murdered repeatedly, always coming back. Ito, 2005.

comics|torso.synopsis: A 2021 comic in which a boy gets out of his body, and the second half of the book is his body walking around without him, which is the better half. Stephen L. Thompson, 2021.
comics|torso.shortSynopsis: A boy who gets out of his body, and the body that continues. 2021.

comics|tower-of-god.synopsis: A 2010 webtoon in which a girl who wants to see the top of a tower teams up with a boy who lies constantly, and the structure is a climb. S.I.U., 2010.
comics|tower-of-god.shortSynopsis: A climb up a tower, with a girl and a boy who lies. 2010.

comics|transmetropolitan.synopsis: A 1997 comic in which a reporter is given a column to write a rant he was fired for, and the rant is the most intelligent thing in the book, and the artwork is why it is still readable. Warren Ellis and Darick Robertson, 1997.
comics|transmetropolitan.shortSynopsis: A reporter given a column to write the rant he was fired for. 1997.

comics|trees.synopsis: A 2018 comic in which the branches of a tree are the paths of lives and the trunk is a wound, and there is no text until the last page. Dash Shaw, 2018.
comics|trees.shortSynopsis: Branches as lives, a trunk as a wound, and no text until the end. 2018.

comics|true-beauty.synopsis: A 2016 webtoon about a woman who is regarded as beautiful and treated as a decoration, and the book is about what she does with that. 2016.
comics|true-beauty.shortSynopsis: A woman treated as a decoration, and what she does. 2016.

comics|two-gun-kid.synopsis: A 1948 Dell western in which the hero is a man who cannot be frightened, which is the era's whole idea of heroism, and he is not frightened of anything including a fall. From 1948.
comics|two-gun-kid.shortSynopsis: A man who cannot be frightened, of anything. 1948.

comics|under-the-oak-tree.synopsis: A 2017 comic in which a girl raised by a family that has never let her near the world is handed the inheritance that makes her leave, and it is a book about grooming. From 2017.
comics|under-the-oak-tree.shortSynopsis: A girl raised away from the world, and the inheritance. 2017.

comics|unknown-soldier.synopsis: A 2014 comic in which a soldier returns to a country he cannot be recalled to, and the book is about the country having moved on without it. Joshua Dysart, 2014.
comics|unknown-soldier.shortSynopsis: A soldier returned to a country that moved on. 2014.

comics|unordinary.synopsis: A 2012 webcomic in which two teenagers can see how much everybody around them lies, and the book is about whether knowing that helps. 2012.
comics|unordinary.shortSynopsis: Two teenagers who can see how much everyone lies. 2012.

comics|unsounded.synopsis: A 2014 webcomic in which a girl who is deaf and a boy who will not speak, and the whole strip is their two languages not meeting. From 2014.
comics|unsounded.shortSynopsis: A deaf girl and a boy who will not speak. 2014.

comics|uzumaki.synopsis: A 1996 manga in which a family moves into a house shaped like a snail and the house is fine, and the book is about what is in it. Junji Ito, 1996.
comics|uzumaki.shortSynopsis: A family in a snail-shaped house, and what is in it. Ito, 1996.

comics|v-for-vendetta.synopsis: A 1988 comic in which a man in a costume sets out to overturn a government, and the argument for doing it with violence is made well enough that it is still argued about. Alan Moore and David Lloyd, 1988.
comics|v-for-vendetta.shortSynopsis: A man in a costume overturning a government, argued seriously. 1988.

comics|vagabond.synopsis: A 1998 manga in which the strongest swordsman alive loses a fight to a woman who is better, and the whole book is the rest of his life. Takehiko Inoue, 1998.
comics|vagabond.shortSynopsis: The strongest swordsman loses to a woman who is better. Inoue, 1998.

comics|valerian-and-laureline.synopsis: A 1967 Franco-Belgian comic in which two time travellers are not chosen and not special, and the galaxy's problems are solved by procedure, and nothing since has been better at science fiction. Pierre Christin and Jean-Claude Mézières, 1967.
comics|valerian-and-laureline.shortSynopsis: Two unchosen time travellers solving things by procedure. 1967.

comics|velvet.synopsis: A 2003 comic in which a man dressed as a woman gets mistaken for a woman, and the book is about a family and a dead relative rather than the mistake. Cathy Hughes, 2003.
comics|velvet.shortSynopsis: A man mistaken for a woman, and a family instead. 2003.

comics|vietnamerica.synopsis: A 2011 graphic novel in which a young American man in Vietnam turns out to be Vietnamese, and the book is about a war that was not what he was told. GB Tran, 2011.
comics|vietnamerica.shortSynopsis: An American in Vietnam who turns out to be Vietnamese. 2011.

comics|villains-are-destined-to-die.synopsis: A 2020 comic in which a woman with a healing factor cannot be killed either way, and the book is about that. From 2020.
comics|villains-are-destined-to-die.shortSynopsis: A woman who cannot be killed either way. 2020.

comics|vinland-saga.synopsis: The manga, which is the same work as the anime entry in this catalogue, and the original is 2005, and the premise is a Viking who was a conqueror and then has to live. Makoto Yukimura, 2005.
comics|vinland-saga.shortSynopsis: A Viking who conquered and then had to live. Yukimura, 2005.

comics|wake.synopsis: A 2007 comic in which a dead man narrates a murder in a town where nothing happens, and he is the only one who knows who did it. Scott Snyder and Sean Murphy, 2007.
comics|wake.shortSynopsis: A dead man narrating a murder nobody else knows about. 2007.

comics|waltz-with-bashir.synopsis: A 2008 graphic novel in which the narrator cannot remember a night of the Lebanon war and the film spends most of its length on why. Ari Folman and David Polonsky, 2008.
comics|waltz-with-bashir.shortSynopsis: A narrator who cannot remember a night of war, and why. 2008.

comics|war-is-boring.synopsis: A 2010 comic in which a British soldier tells a child what war is actually like, without softening it, and the child is his son. Garth Ennis, 2010.
comics|war-is-boring.shortSynopsis: A British soldier telling his child what war is really like. 2010.

comics|war-stories.synopsis: A 2001 comic in which each issue is one soldier's war and no two soldiers are on the same side, and the series' whole argument is in the ordering. Garth Ennis, 2001.
comics|war-stories.shortSynopsis: One soldier's war per issue, no two on the same side. 2001.

comics|warlord-of-mars.synopsis: A 1940 comic in which the character is a Confederate soldier who wakes up on Mars as a sixteen-year-old boy, and the book was also a novel, a film and a radio serial. Edgar Rice Burroughs, 1940.
comics|warlord-of-mars.shortSynopsis: A Confederate soldier awake on Mars as a boy. 1940.

comics|wasteland.synopsis: A 1988 comic in which a father and daughter walk across a post-nuclear America arguing about whether it was worth it, and the book is the argument. Alan Dwight, 1988.
comics|wasteland.shortSynopsis: A father and daughter crossing post-nuclear America, arguing. 1988.

comics|watchmen.synopsis: A 1986 comic in which masked crimefighters stopped existing and the trade-union organiser was the most powerful person in the country, and the book is about a murder investigation. Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons, 1986.
comics|watchmen.shortSynopsis: Masked heroes gone, a union organiser in power, and a murder. 1986.

comics|watchmen-literary.synopsis: The same 1986 work as the row above, held separately because the importer split the title on a genre qualifier. Same work, and the qualifier is the argument.
comics|watchmen-literary.shortSynopsis: The same work as watchmen, split on a genre qualifier. A duplicate row.

comics|we-stand-on-guard.synopsis: A 2015 comic in which protected superhumans are obliged to sit on a council and do nothing about anything, and the book is the meeting. Matt Wagner, 2015.
comics|we-stand-on-guard.shortSynopsis: Superhumans on a council obliged to do nothing. 2015.

comics|wednesday-comics.synopsis: A 2013 DC anthology in which each week a different artist takes a different DC character, and the line between them was so thin the fans turned it into a game. DC, 2013.
comics|wednesday-comics.shortSynopsis: A different artist and character each week, and a fan game. 2013.

comics|weird-tales.synopsis: A 1923 pulp magazine in which the cover art was better than the stories and the circulation depended on the covers, and the stories in the good issues are first-rate. From 1923.
