kpop|lee-nan-young.shortSynopsis: Warm and unhurried, and deliberately small.
kpop|lee-nan-young.synopsis: A South Korean singer-songwriter with a warm, unhurried delivery who writes about ordinary relationships and has stayed deliberately small.

kpop|lee-seung-chul.shortSynopsis: A broadcast career, and better than expected.
kpop|lee-seung-chul.synopsis: A South Korean singer and television personality who has had a career almost entirely in broadcast, and who sings better than the format usually allows a television personality to sing.

kpop|lee-sun-hee.synopsis: A South Korean singer from the 2000s who had a serious voice and a serious recording career that ended early, and she is a reference point rather than an ongoing act.
kpop|lee-sun-hee.shortSynopsis: A serious 2000s career that ended early.

kpop|lim-han-byeol.shortSynopsis: Into electronic and ambient, which the group forbade.
kpop|lim-han-byeol.synopsis: A South Korean artist who came from a girl group and whose solo work moved deliberately into electronic and ambient territory, which the group would not have permitted.

kpop|lim-jae-hyun.shortSynopsis: The strongest vocalist in a group that ended.
kpop|lim-jae-hyun.synopsis: A South Korean singer who is a member of a boy group and who was regarded as the strongest vocalist in his group before the group ended.

kpop|love-x-stereo.shortSynopsis: Warm, club-ready, and made for the cuts.
kpop|love-x-stereo.synopsis: A South Korean electronic duo whose name is a pun on a stereo, and whose music is warm and club-ready and made for the format's choreography cuts.

kpop|loveholics.shortSynopsis: The more conventional of the two co-ed projects.
kpop|loveholics.synopsis: A South Korean group that followed the co-ed unit in this catalogue and kept the same name, and which is the more conventional of the two.

kpop|m-i-l-k.shortSynopsis: Deliberately flat and sample-heavy, rejecting brightness.
kpop|m-i-l-k.synopsis: A South Korean electronic act that makes a deliberately flat, sample-heavy sound, and the flatness is a rejection of the format's usual brightness.

kpop|naul-gummy.shortSynopsis: The same artist as gummy and naul, under two names. A duplicate row.
kpop|naul-gummy.synopsis: The same artist as two rows in this catalogue held under the collaborative and solo names, and the two rows are one person. Same work.

kpop|no-brain.shortSynopsis: A self-deprecating name on funny, low-stakes work.
kpop|no-brain.synopsis: A South Korean hip hop artist whose name is self-deprecating and whose work is a deliberately simple, low-stakes, funny thing that contradicts the name.

kpop|nrg.shortSynopsis: A shifting lineup that lasted for decades.
kpop|nrg.synopsis: A South Korean male vocal group formed in 1997 that survived for decades with a shifting lineup, and the longevity is the achievement.

kpop|papaya.shortSynopsis: An absurd early concept, now carefully made.
kpop|papaya.synopsis: A South Korean group whose name is a fruit and whose early concept was deliberately absurd, and who are now much more carefully made than the name suggests.

kpop|park-hyo-shin.shortSynopsis: Plain, about work and money, and refuses to impress.
kpop|park-hyo-shin.synopsis: A South Korean singer-songwriter with a very plain delivery who writes about work and money and has a large following for a singer who refuses to be impressive.

kpop|park-hyun-bin.shortSynopsis: A serious acting career and a better singer than it needs.
kpop|park-hyun-bin.synopsis: A South Korean singer who has a serious acting career and a music career that mostly serves it, and who is a much better singer than the arrangement of her career suggests.

kpop|peppertones.shortSynopsis: Sunshine pop, with naivety as construction.
kpop|peppertones.synopsis: A South Korean band that plays sunshine pop with deliberate naivety, and the naivety is carefully constructed rather than naive.

kpop|rooftop-moonlight.synopsis: A South Korean indie band that makes quiet, nocturnal music and is a cult act here without ever charting.

kpop|royal-pirates.shortSynopsis: Pirates, and a very old joke about it.
kpop|royal-pirates.synopsis: A South Korean group with a name that describes both their name-appropriation habit and their actual pirate-themed concept, and the joke is very old.

kpop|sg-wannabe.shortSynopsis: Deliberately early-2000s loud, as an argument.
kpop|sg-wannabe.synopsis: A South Korean girl group formed in 2022 with a deliberately loud, early-2000s girl-group sound, and the label treated it as retro and it functioned as an argument.

kpop|shark.shortSynopsis: From the pre-idol indie scene the format absorbed.
kpop|shark.synopsis: A South Korean group that came from the underground, and which is an early instance of the pre-idol indie scene that the format has since absorbed.

kpop|shin-yong-jae.shortSynopsis: The most technically precise act from that show.
kpop|shin-yong-jae.synopsis: A South Korean rapper who came out of a televised rap competition and who is regarded as the most technically precise of that competition's output.

kpop|sirup.shortSynopsis: Considered the best here, and never on a major label.
kpop|sirup.synopsis: A South Korean hip hop producer and rapper who came from the underground, is considered one of the best in the country, and has never signed to a major label.

kpop|slom.shortSynopsis: Hazy and ambient, with no category in the format.
kpop|slom.synopsis: A South Korean artist whose name is a deliberate misspelling, and whose work is a hazy, slow, ambient thing that the format has no category for.

kpop|ssingssing.shortSynopsis: Old-fashioned rock the format has no place for.
kpop|ssingssing.synopsis: A South Korean duo whose name is an onomatopoeia, and which makes an affectionate, deliberately old-fashioned rock that the format has no place for and which has consequently survived.

kpop|sung-hoon.shortSynopsis: The group's strongest dancer, with a separate solo interest.
kpop|sung-hoon.synopsis: A South Korean singer who is a member of a boy group and is regarded within it as the strongest dancer, and who has released solo material that is a small, separate interest.

kpop|sweet-sorrow.shortSynopsis: Three people, small and consistent, for most of its life.
kpop|sweet-sorrow.synopsis: A South Korean rock band formed in 2007 that has been the same three people for most of its life and that plays a small, consistent, unfashionable thing.

kpop|the-poles.shortSynopsis: Abrasive rock, under various names, for a long time.
kpop|the-poles.synopsis: A South Korean indie band that plays noisy, abrasive rock and has existed under various names for a long time.

kpop|the-volunteers.shortSynopsis: The most openly political scene in the country.
kpop|the-volunteers.synopsis: A South Korean group whose name states its own politics, and which came out of the scene that had been most openly political in the country.

kpop|third-mind.shortSynopsis: One of the most sophisticated of the 2002 scene.
kpop|third-mind.synopsis: A South Korean hip hop group formed in 2002 that is regarded as one of the most musically sophisticated of that era's scene, and which is analytically cool rather than popular.

kpop|trans-fixion.shortSynopsis: An avant-garde name on approachable music.
kpop|trans-fixion.synopsis: A South Korean group with a deliberately avant-garde name, and whose music is more approachable than the name promises, which is a recurring pattern here.

kpop|weightless.shortSynopsis: Spaced-out and drifting, and the name is the concept.
kpop|weightless.synopsis: A South Korean band that plays spaced-out, drifting music and whose name is the entire concept.

kpop|wonstein.shortSynopsis: A theatrical high voice, and a character.
kpop|wonstein.synopsis: A South Korean musician and television personality with a very high, theatrical voice who is a character rather than a conventional performer.

kpop|yang-hee-eun.shortSynopsis: Quiet, literary, and outside the machinery.
kpop|yang-hee-eun.synopsis: A South Korean singer-songwriter whose work is quiet, literary and long-running, and who has stayed out of the format's machinery entirely.

kpop|yellow-monsters.shortSynopsis: An unpleasant name on bright pop-punk.
kpop|yellow-monsters.synopsis: A South Korean band whose name is deliberately unpleasant and whose music is a bright, fast, pop-punk thing, which is the whole joke and it works.

kpop|yellow-ocean.synopsis: A South Korean indie act that makes warm, hazy music and is small and long-running.

kpop|yoon-ji-sung.shortSynopsis: Plain and unhurried, which the group would not make.
kpop|yoon-ji-sung.synopsis: A South Korean singer-songwriter who came from a girl group and whose solo work is a plain, unhurried, small thing that the group would not have made.

kpop|chaeyoung.synopsis: A South Korean singer who is a member of a girl group, who also publishes photography books, and who is the member the group is most often said to be built around.
kpop|chaeyoung.shortSynopsis: A group member who is also a published photographer.

kpop|homme.synopsis: A South Korean musician who is the singer and guitarist of an indie band, and who writes the band's material and is the reason the band sounds the way it does rather than generic.
kpop|homme.shortSynopsis: The singer-writer of that indie band, and the reason it sounds like itself.

kpop|adoy.synopsis: A South Korean rock band formed in 2016 that became the most-played new rock act on Korean streaming radio, and the streaming-radio route is how a great many of the country's bands now reach an audience.
kpop|adoy.shortSynopsis: The most-played new rock act on Korean streaming radio.

kpop|junoflo.synopsis: A South Korean producer and songwriter who has produced a large share of the softer, more literate songs in this catalogue, and who is a musician before he is a producer of other people.
kpop|junoflo.shortSynopsis: Produced much of the softer, more literate material here.

kpop|sam-kim.synopsis: A South Korean-American singer who came from a televised singing competition and who subsequently became a recording artist in her own right, and who is the strongest thing the format has produced in that pipeline.
kpop|sam-kim.shortSynopsis: From a televised competition into a recording career.

kpop|sam-lewis.synopsis: A South Korean-American singer-songwriter who competed in a televised singing competition and who went on to a songwriting career, and the songwriting is the more substantial half.
kpop|sam-lewis.shortSynopsis: A competition entry who became a songwriter.

kpop|diva.synopsis: A South Korean artist who came out of a televised singing competition and whose voice is the reason she is in this catalogue rather than her release history.
kpop|diva.shortSynopsis: A competition entry, remembered for the voice.
